06365: A mechanical crossbow. It attacks enemies who come close on its own, and is one of the main targets of enemy puppet soldiers.
06372: Mu Yijian is a highly skilled hunter. He spends year after year roaming the mountain forests and knows the habits of every kind of prey like the back of his hand. With his excellent hunting skills, he always comes back with a full load. He shares his catch with the people around him, so everyone likes him. In this land, Mu Yi is a symbol of courage and wisdom.
06374: Tang Yi was born into a family of blacksmiths who have made their living at the forge for generations. He is strong and has spent years sweating by the furnace. But fate played a trick on him: he is lame in one leg. Even so, he quietly keeps to the craft handed down by his ancestors. Tang Tiefeng says little and focuses only on the hammer and iron in his hands, forging one fine piece of ironwork after another.
06375: Dong Jianghuan is a student at a private school who showed extraordinary intelligence from a young age. He always handles his studies with ease and is much praised by his teacher. But having been spoiled, he hates physical work. Even for simple tasks he has no patience, wanting only to bury himself in the world of knowledge.
06377: Liu Shu is a simple farmer. He spends his days with the land and is very good at farming. Life is poor and hard, but he loves it and works with passion. The hard conditions have shaped his tough character; whatever setbacks he meets, he faces them bravely and never backs down.
06379: Zou Tiefeng is an old bachelor in the village. He is handsome and has a certain grace. But fate seems to have played a joke on him: for all his fine looks, he is small and thin, born with a hunched back, and can only make a living doing odd jobs nearby. Even so, he is responsible in all he does and has the villagers' trust.
06381: Zheng Yidao the butcher is a slab of muscle with superb knife skills. He secretly carried a torch for the Widow Zhang next door, and always cut her an extra measure of meat. Then one day a local tyrant ran wild, and she was killed. The quick knife he used every day to carve up oxen became a blade of revenge. That night, Butcher Zheng went out knife in hand; blood splashed the long street, and the tyrant's whole household was slaughtered. With it done, he brushed off his clothes, vanished into the deep mountains and was never seen again.
06383: The world's muddy currents run strong. No one remembers the name Qin Kuai anymore; only the words "King Yama Qin" still make people shudder. He was once a mounted constable, but his upright nature didn't sit well with a corrupt world; he was framed, stripped of his post and drifted into the jianghu as a hired blade. Now he seems indifferent and takes only paid jobs, but when he sees the weak and helpless being bullied, that narrow saber of his is always faster than his reason. In a flash of the blade, you can see that the hard-nosed officer who hated evil like a foe never went far.
06385: Chi Nu was a merchant from the Western Regions. Years ago he led a camel train south, only to be robbed of everything by bandits on the way. He survived the disaster and escaped to the city, where yamen runners put him in iron chains and sent him to repair a breach in the Yellow River. Then came a natural disaster in which nine out of ten died, but Chi Nu lived. He never dared go back to the city again, and so, to survive, he ended up a roving bandit.
06387: A lone wandering swordsman carrying a blood feud for his family. His scabbard is old, yet it hides the divine blade "Startled Swan", and he never hesitates to strike. He has worn half an iron mask for years, and the jianghu calls him "Ghost-Faced Hong". In truth he hides guilt over his past, and in the final duel with his old enemy he chooses to let go of hatred rather than drown in killing.
06388: Huang Xianglan is an excellent cook. The food she makes is praised for miles around. She is clever, and her warm, generous manner makes people feel at home. Day after day in the kitchen sometimes wears on her, but she sticks with it, winning everyone over with her delicious food.
06390: Tang Yingxia is a girl full of curiosity about the world. She is frank and bold, doesn't fuss over small things, and can make friends with all walks of life. Through this, she joined an obscure little sect and learned some fist and kick skills. But her single-minded stubbornness often gives her master headaches, which keeps her from studying the martial arts in depth.
06392: Liu Rushi is a woman who goes her own way. She is wrapped up in solitude and loves only the quiet of night. She is sharp-tongued; to her, only herself and her carving are worth attention in this world. Though she often seems cold, she hides a gentle hope inside: that someone will give her their heart, and her alone for life, walking the long road of life with her and guarding her pride and talent.
06394: Su Ying showed extraordinary intelligence from childhood, with a remarkable grasp of medicines and a thorough command of pharmacology. She uses medicine skillfully on herself to sharpen her focus and keep her rest sound. Her superb medical skill and striking beauty are widely known; everyone calls her the Beautiful Doctor, and patients come one after another, hoping her skilled hands will bring them back to health.
06396: Ban Tang was born a natural beauty and was once a famous courtesan in the capital. She is courteous and speaks with great finesse; every frown and smile is captivating. But she is physically frail and can't handle physical labor, which brings some helplessness to her life, yet she still gives off a charm all her own.
06398: She is Li Lankou, the orphan of a general's house. After her family was destroyed, the once-cherished daughter fell into the jianghu. She is no longer anyone's precious young lady; all she has left is a bow, a quiver of arrows and a heart soaked in hatred. She draws her bow round as the full moon, and her arrows fly like shooting stars; wherever the bowstring sounds, someone dies. This is a road of revenge that belongs to her alone.
06400: Hu Pan'er is a fine dancer, and best of all at puppet shows: with silk threads she makes marionettes act out every joy and sorrow. The world thinks it only a stage trick, not knowing how many traitors and villains she has finished off with this art. She says: "In these chaotic times, who isn't a puppet? And I am only the dancer who sends the puppet-masters to their graves."
06402: The daughter of the leader of the Western Regions sabersmen. She wields a curved saber called "Cold Moon" and is decisive and spirited. Investigating her father's death, she has crossed blades with Ye Jinghong many times. She once believed "revenge is justice", but in her dealings with Ye Jinghong she gradually came to understand the true meaning of "settling scores with a clear heart". In the end, the two went from opponents to close friends fighting side by side.
06404: A troop of soldiers escorting a pine coffin passes through the Post Station, looking panicked. The coffin looks ordinary, but it is bound with ink lines and pasted with talisman paper. They refuse all conversation and shy away from the coffin, as if what lies inside is not the dead but some living thing that terrifies them, and even they are afraid of disturbing the "thing" within.
06407: Villagers carry a small blue cloth sedan chair into the Post Station. Their eyes dart away, and they won't say a word about what's inside. The curtain's seams are sealed with wet cloth, and a sticky, watery sound drifts out on the night wind. When the watchman's clapper sounds midnight, the chair shakes harder and harder, as if something terrible is about to burst out.
06409: Once this run is done, I'll have the money to take a wife back home... shh
06410: Formerly Hall Master of the Tianji Sect's Nandou Hall, an upright man who acts openly. He lost his wife in middle age and has no children of his own; watching the young Sect Master grow up day by day, he treats them as his own and dotes on them.
06411: Formerly Hall Master of the Tianji Sect's Tianshi Hall, in charge of the sect's money, intelligence and similar affairs. He went through life and death with the old Sect Master, and in the battle of Wangyue Peak chose to stay behind with the other members to fight off the enemy.
06412: Formerly Hall Master of the Tianji Sect's Beidou Hall, in charge of the sect's punishments. He keeps public and private strictly apart and hates evil like a sworn enemy. His whereabouts have been unknown since the battle of Wangyue Peak.
06413: Formerly Sect Master of the Tianji Sect and also Hall Master of Ziwei Hall, overseeing every affair of the sect, great and small. When Wangyue Peak was besieged, he sent everyone away and stayed behind alone to cover their retreat; the sect's members all believe he died long ago.
06414: Formerly Hall Master of the Tianji Sect's Taiwei Hall, in charge of the sect's rules and regulations, and Yuchi Xiao's senior brother. He always greets people with a smile and seems very kind and approachable; only the older disciples know his temper is anything but ordinary.
06415: A Taiji master long famous in the jianghu, resting here a while on his travels. The Post Station is noisy, but even that can't drown out the master's shouting: "Have any of you seen my famous ultimate move, the Lightning Five-Whip Combo? Once I use it, I'm afraid no one under heaven can stand against me."
06416: He always wears a long moon-white robe with clean cuffs. His features are gentle, and when he smiles he looks like the young scholar next door; no one would guess he was once a scholar who failed the exams. That year he lost everything and put himself up as the stake. Now he stands behind the gambling table; when he shuffles, his fingertips move as lightly as if playing a zither, but his eyes are as cold as a scale weighing bones. When he wins, he nods slightly; when he loses, he nods slightly too. He's more unnerving when he isn't smiling than when he is.
06418: Place your bets and hands off... Opening, opening!
06419: The newly crowned top assassin under heaven. He firmly believes that "of all the martial arts under heaven, only speed cannot be beaten". Inspired by a toad catching its prey, he wants to create a toad skill of his own, and so he travels everywhere looking for inspiration.
06420: The Post Station falls suddenly silent. Everyone stares at the bamboo hat in the corner and the broad ghost-head saber on his back. The air is heavy as iron. They know that capturing this man is worth a thousand in gold, but though his blade hasn't moved, killing intent has already soaked into the beams. In the end, no one dares take that step.
06421: A three-foot wooden table, a cup of tea and a fan. The storyteller gently waves his folding fan, yet the tea on the corner of the table shows not a single ripple.
06424: Shelves crammed full of goods. The merchant wears an innocent smile, wiping the sweat from his brow as he calls out his wares.
06426: Walk on by and you'll miss out! Selling cheap here; a few coins buys what your heart desires. Come on, hurry up!
06428: A country girl of sixteen, very fresh and pretty. Sadly, the bud withered before it could bloom; what a pity.
06431: The book stall isn't big, but its shelves have everything. Sword manuals sit next to cookbooks, and erotic pictures are tucked under prescriptions. Passers-by find it messy; he doesn't explain, just keeps his head down in his own book. Only when someone who knows quality crouches down to dig through the bottom of a box does he look up once, then lower his head again.
06433: Rare books and fine editions, sole copies and handwritten copies! Gentlemen who know quality, look this way; once you pass this village there's no such shop!
06435: The owner of the equipment shop never asks where things come from. A bandit's saber, a constable's sword, a breastplate pawned by some jianghu type: he takes it all. When he sells them on, he doesn't ask what they're for either. When people tell him to watch out for trouble, he just chuckles: "Weapons are made of iron and people are made of flesh. Who causes trouble for whom isn't settled yet."
06437: Sabers, spears, swords, halberds, axes, hooks and forks, all made with our family's ancestral craft. If it comes out crooked, that's on me! Want a sword, sir? If it can't cut anyone, you can still use it as a mirror!
06439: The Post Station's resident storyteller. He has spent years roaming the streets gathering jianghu anecdotes, has an excellent memory and can tell all kinds of strange tales in loving detail. He hasn't the strength to truss a chicken, but he has plenty of ways of getting information, telling jianghu stories in exchange for travel money. He is smooth with people, and now and then asks for a little something for his trouble before he'll reveal the inside story.
06441: As the story goes, the clash of those two masters echoed through the valley, waking a Fire Qilin that had slept for hundreds of years......
06442: In a scholar's robe, gently waving a folding fan, standing tall as a pine and speaking with refined grace: what a dashing young gentleman.
06444: Born into a family of officials with a spotless reputation. He is tall and powerfully built, upright and stern, and through his outstanding ability rose to become Chief Constable of the Six Doors, leading the pursuit of fugitives across the land; he is the court's sharp blade against the most vicious criminals.
06446: Cool and aloof, living year-round in a secluded valley. Her white clothes outshine the snow and her swordsmanship is beyond compare. Indifferent by nature, yet she values kindness and loyalty; like an otherworldly immortal beauty who does not eat the food of the mortal world.
06447: Zhao Huo wears shining armor, has superb martial skill and says little. He has long stayed at the jianghu Post Station, as if secretly investigating the truth of some little-known old case
06448: White-haired, in a beggar's robe, he loves good food and wine. Bold and carefree by nature, with unfathomable martial arts, he roams the jianghu punishing evil and promoting good. He seems easygoing, but holds great righteousness in his heart.
06450: A knight from a foreign land in the far west, clad in plate armor and holding a great sword, speaking strangely. He strayed into this jianghu by mistake and is looking for the way back to his homeland.
06452: This man deals only with jianghu folk and never stays put: in one city today, who knows where tomorrow. His rules are odd: he doesn't put his good things on display; you have to ask, and then he brings them out. Ask how he knows what you're after, and he says: "Twenty years in this trade. I can tell at a glance what kind of person goes with what kind of goods."
06453: Mountain goods and local produce you won't find anywhere else! Go to a big shop in the city and spend ten times the silver, and you still won't get what I've got. It's not that they won't sell it; they simply don't have it!
06455: A monk from the Western Regions stands proudly in the middle of the Post Station, his red-and-yellow robe stirring with no wind. His green eyes sweep the room, and in broken Mandarin he boasts: "The martial arts of the Central Plains are all empty fame!" With that he strikes the floor with his Chan staff, and the blue bricks crack. The jianghu folk in the hall rise with hands on their swords, only to see the cold gleam of a golden wheel already showing in his sleeve.
06456: A warrior from Dongying perches in a corner of the Post Station like a black crow, wrapped head to toe in night-walker's clothes with only a pair of sharp eyes showing, roaming the room. He sits curled up with a hand on his wakizashi, like a venomous spider guarding its web. Travelers all go around him, and even the post horses stamp their iron hooves uneasily as they pass.
06457: Mo Qianji is the sixth generation of the direct Mohist line, ingenious from a young age. Before he came of age, an elder brought a thin, dark vagrant boy into the school, who spent all day buried in the library until everyone nearly forgot he existed. On the night Qianji was to become head of the Mohists, the library caught fire, and the thin dark youth broke out on an ingenious mechanical beast. As he left, he looked down on them all, but gazed at Qianji alone for a long time. Qianji then gave up the position of head and went down the mountain, searching for him for twenty years.
06459: Covered in talisman paper and locked tight with fine iron chains. Something extraordinary seems to be lying inside.
06460: An open coffin, completely empty, giving off waves of stench. It looks like something has escaped from it.
06461: The curtain's seams are sealed with wet cloth, and a sticky, watery sound drifts out on the night wind.
06462: Dark-faced with a curly beard, in short work clothes with a belted waist. He loves tobacco and wine and is fiery and bold; on the Bian River docks no one dares stand against his iron fists. In his early years he ran salt and escorted boats up and down the river, used to wind, waves and danger, and later settled at Kaifeng's water gate as foreman.
06464: Listen up, all of you! The work went smoothly today, and not one ship owner found anything to complain about! Pack up your gear and come to my shed. Tonight there's stewed river fish and warm old wine. Drink all you like!
06466: Lean and dark, bare-chested and in straw sandals, with a black bamboo carrying pole worn glossy and a thick callus on his shoulder from years of loads. Three generations of his family were porters on the Bian River; from the Zhou Bridge docks to the front of Xiangguo Temple, there's no road for miles around he doesn't know.
06467: I've carried more goods than there are fish in the Bian River!
06468: Blue clothes and a small cap, waving a folding fan, with a polished brass abacus tucked in his belt. He grew up in a warehouse; at eight he could quote the going price of every kind of goods in Kaifeng, and his sharp tongue could talk a dead duck into a live chicken. He has a keen eye; one glance at the goods in his hands tells him their quality and price.
06470: Say what you like, but the ways of the docks and the truth about the goods, I can lay them out for you clearly with my eyes closed!
06471: "I don't sell to strangers, only to those fated to buy." She never hurries a customer, because she knows that those who truly need these masks will see their own heart's desires or fears through these fierce faces. She has kept her stall here for thirty years; the moss on the blue brick wall beside it has grown back countless times, yet she still keeps watch over this crowd of gods and demons.
06473: A life is just a skin you wear. Change your face, and you change your way of living.
06474: Having seen people come and go in this deep alley for years, she knows all the town's household gossip, weddings and funerals. Whose master is taking a concubine, whose young lady is about to elope; nothing escapes her eyes.
06476: Oh! Do come in, sir! Look at the fine silks in this deep alley. Freshly arrived Hangzhou gauze, breezy and cool for summer!
06477: The biggest sign here is the two huge bronze gongs at the door. Master Lei set the rules: one strike of the gong, trading begins; two strikes, goods and silver have changed hands; three strikes, no credit. He never judges people by their looks; he only cares who pays the most silver and who brings the best goods.
06479: Brother, I don't know your face. What good stuff is in your bundle? Whatever it is, bring it out and let me have a look.
06480: The shopkeeper has run this shop for years, selling dried goods from north and south, aged tea and some ingredients for medicinal dishes. He has his own old steelyard with the marks worn shiny, is very picky about his goods and hates it most when people say his wares aren't genuine. He usually keeps a straight face, but with an old customer who knows the trade, he shows a warmth as rare as an iron rooster losing a feather.
06482: Genuine aged tea, hand-picked dried fruit and well-aged medicinal wine, all right here on this counter!
06484: Knowing stage makeup, she worked out her own secret recipes for rouge and powder; her "Peach Blossom Tipsy" and "Crimson Lips" can make even a poor family's girl glow with wealth. She has a woman's finest sensibilities. Besides selling cosmetics, she does the hair and makeup for every bride-to-be in town. She has a keen eye: one glance at a customer coming in and she can tell whether the girl wants to please a man or outshine a rival.
06486: Ah, for a woman, the color on her face is her protective charm. She has to keep a firm grip on her own capital.
06487: The waiter has worked at this restaurant for eight years. Not only does he remember the tastes of most of the town's customers (who loves spicy food, who can't drink, who likes it quiet, who loves gossip most), he has also grown a pair of "flying legs": carrying a few plates of hot dishes up the twisting stairs at a run, he doesn't spill a drop of soup.
06489: Welcome, hero! You look travel-worn. By jianghu custom, how about I bring you a big bowl of Nu'er Hong first and slice two jin of cooked beef to line your stomach? If that's not enough, there's more; we'll fill you up!
06490: He has been a constable in this town for fifteen years and knows the town's black market inside out: he knows Master Lei's general store secretly takes stolen goods, that Wang Xiaojiu at the restaurant has the best information, that Caigu's rouge shop sometimes passes secret signals to jianghu folk, and that Aunt Meng's masks can guard a house against evil. But he never interferes much, because he knows full well that "water too clear holds no fish".
06492: Don't get anyone killed on my beat. Anything else, I'll turn a blind eye, as long as you slip me a little information.
06493: She was a cook for a wealthy family in her early years, and later set up a stall of her own. Her pastries look lovely and taste wonderful. She's a chatterbox who likes gossiping with the neighbors while she wraps her dumplings, and she's the town's second-best source of news.
06495: Osmanthus cakes fresh from the steamer! Hot red bean buns, plump white glutinous rice cakes! If it's not tasty, it's free! Don't walk past and miss out: one bite is sweet enough to rot your teeth; take some home to please your wife!
06496: He was a soldier in his early years and retired after a serious wound. He bought a barren hilltop outside the city and, with his own two hands, planted fruit trees all over it. He has carried fruit into the city on his shoulder pole for twenty years. He may only sell fruit, but he has a sharp eye: in a crowd he can tell at a glance who's truly rich and who's just putting on a show.
06498: Fruit from my own hill, crisp, sweet and juicy. Come have a look.
06499: The jianghu calls him the "Smiling Tiger". When young he was only a small bookkeeper, but during a great drought he used his position to mix sand and moldy rice into the relief grain, killing many of the starving, and made a fortune from that black money. Later he bought himself an empty honorary post and took over the Fengyu Grain Store, the biggest in town.
06501: Oh my, honored guests at the door, honored guests at the door! Our store's newly arrived tribute rice, plump grains with a fragrance that carries for miles! Please come in, please come in. Lu at your service!
06502: He's a true "jianghu wanderer" with no fixed shop, pushing a wheelbarrow or carrying a basket from one river and road port to the next year-round. He has been to the miasmic lands of the south and the bitter cold frontier beyond the passes. His greatest skill isn't just having every kind of goods, but having a clever tongue. Those few bamboo darts in his hand are actually his "customer magnets": he draws a circle on the Sky Bridge and sets up a little pitch-pot and dart game. Hit the target and you get a trinket for free; miss and you have to buy his goods. With the dart game he draws a crowd, and then naturally starts selling.
06504: Whatever's in my basket, if you can think of it, I can bring it out!
06506: The only daughter of a Jiangnan family of kite makers. Her family fell on hard times when she was young, and she drifted here alone with the family's bamboo-strip craft and secret color recipes, and took over this shop. Her craft is superb: the frames are perfectly balanced and the painting is outstanding. The cranes she paints seem to break through the clouds, and the butterflies' wings seem to carry morning dew.
06508: The kite flies into the clouds, and worries go with the wind. Feel free to look at the kites; if you're buying, name your price.
06509: He drifted here after misfortune struck his family. He has no great skills except brewing a fine cup of tea. He has had this tea stall set up next to the kite shop for nearly a year now, just to catch a few more glimpses of that lovely figure each day.
06511: D-don't joke around! I, I just think Miss Qingshang is a refined person, and my tea stall happens to be close by, handy for helping her business a little... What's all this about admiring her? It'd be embarrassing if she heard. Am I still selling tea or not...
06513: His ancestors included a Hanlin scholar, but by his generation the family had declined. In his early years he went to the capital for the exams full of ambition, but was secretly struck off the list for refusing to bribe the chief examiner. Disheartened, he gave up all thought of office for good, and carrying an old zither, traveled south from the north until he set up a calligraphy and painting stall in this town.
06515: Everyone says calligraphy and painting are worth a thousand in gold, not knowing that a thousand in gold can't buy the meaning in a painting. I, Wuding, have drifted half my life and made my home everywhere; what I paint is the flash of blades, what I play is joy and sorrow, meeting and parting. If my paintings sold, I'd have been a rich merchant long ago. Sadly, my paintings are only for those fated to have them.
06516: A son of a fallen Jiangnan family who once was rich. His ancestors left many old things, but unwilling to live off his inheritance until it was gone, he took up trading antiques. He is very good at dressing himself up and takes the path of "culture feeds commerce": he always carries some tattered book for show and spins half-true, nonsensical tales of his "ancestral glory" for customers.
06518: Come and look, come and see! Old things from the previous dynasty: calligraphy, paintings, porcelain, bronzes, all fine pieces handed down from my ancestors. Anything that's obviously fake, I, Gu, would never embarrass myself by putting on the table...
06519: As a boy he studied breathing techniques and talismans for a few years with a wandering Daoist, but later lost patience with the monastic rules and roamed north and south with an old cloth bag on his back. He makes a living reading routes for people, writing talismans and telling jianghu tales. He calls himself "Master Daoist", but he knows better than anyone how dangerous the world is.
06520: This poor Daoist roams the four corners; I dare not call my talismans and fortune sticks divine. If you want to know whether the road ahead is lucky or not, first hear me say a few words!
06521: When young he worked as a porter on the docks; the savings he built up were burned to nothing in a big fire, and his legs were left with an old injury. Now he sits begging on the streets of Kaifeng. He knows every alley and every walk of life, and keeps a tally in his head of who passes by and who gives.
06522: This old beggar has nowhere to settle. Be kind and spare a hot meal; I'll tell you which alleys in this city are good for making a living!
06524: An elder of the Beggar Sect known as the "Chess Fanatic". Down on his luck in the jianghu for half his life, he holds court at a tea stall with a pot of tea and a chessboard. He knows open xiangqi, hidden-piece chess and endgame puzzles. Given a handicap he reads the player; playing all-out he reads the board. The rules of chess are the rules of the world: the chariot moves straight, the horse moves in an L, and a person shouldn't go crooked.
06526: Known as "Nimble-Handed Jiang", he was once a peddler who traveled north and south, saw his share of curiosities and trained a pair of clever hands. Later he set up a games stall in the city and draws customers with three specialties: lining up colored beads to clear them, threading needles to knit something warm, and setting black and white stones five in a row to settle a match. He's warm-hearted and never sore about winning or losing: winners get a prize, losers get a laugh. The stall is small but often ringed with passersby, and has become a sight on the street corner.
06532: Mu Yi is a highly skilled hunter. He spends year after year roaming the mountain forests and knows the habits of every kind of prey like the back of his hand. With his excellent hunting skills, he always comes back with a full load. He shares his catch with the people around him, so everyone likes him. In this land, Mu Yi is a symbol of courage and wisdom.
06533: Sorry, we already have a hunter we can trust.
06534: Your bow is just what we need.
06535: Sect Master, my name is Mu Yi. These straw sandals that have walked all over the mountain forests can follow deer tracks to water a li away; this hunting bow, polished bright, knows the hours of every bird and beast. Every hunt I bring back double the game: half for the old and weak at the village entrance, half for the night guards. If you take me in, I'll use these eyes that can see through any stir in the grass to guard every blade of grass and every tree of your sect.
06536: Tang Tiefeng was born into a family of blacksmiths who have made their living at the forge for generations. He is strong and has spent years sweating by the furnace. But fate played a trick on him: he is lame in one leg. Even so, he quietly keeps to the craft handed down by his ancestors. Tang Tiefeng says little and focuses only on the hammer and iron in his hands, forging one fine piece of ironwork after another.
06537: We have enough blacksmiths for now.
06538: The weapon workshop is short of a blacksmith.
06539: Sect Master, my name is Tang Tiefeng. This hammer forged iron with my father for thirty years, and even lame as I am, I can still beat quenching patterns into the sparks. On our ancestral anvil, every hammer mark is my promise to the iron.
06540: Dong Shu is a student at a private school who showed extraordinary intelligence from a young age. He always handles his studies with ease and is much praised by his teacher. But having been spoiled, he hates physical work. Even for simple tasks he has no patience, wanting only to bury himself in the world of knowledge.
06541: Of all people, scholars are the most useless!
06542: Learning can also keep the realm safe.
06543: Sect Master, my name is Dong Shu. I can read the whole of the Records of the Grand Historian in three days and solve problems from the Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art. It's just these hands... they're fine holding a brush, but they shake holding a hoe.
06544: Liu Tianding is a simple farmer. He spends his days with the land and is very good at farming. Life is poor and hard, but he loves it and works with passion. The hard conditions have shaped his tough character; whatever setbacks he meets, he faces them bravely and never backs down.
06546: The wasteland is yours. May the granaries be full.
06547: Sect Master, my name is Liu Tianding. This hoe broke open ten mu of barren flats, and three times I covered the seedlings with my straw cape in a downpour. Just give me a patch of soil to take root in, and I'll make ears of wheat sprout even from the cracks in the stones.
06549: Zou Yijian is an old bachelor in the village. He is handsome and has a certain grace. But fate seems to have played a joke on him: for all his fine looks, he is small and thin, born with a hunched back, and can only make a living doing odd jobs nearby. Even so, he is responsible in all he does and has the villagers' trust.
06550: We don't need anyone for now.
06552: Sect Master, my name is Zou Yijian. My hunched back can't carry heavy loads, but I can keep a storehouse in perfect order and work the bookkeeper's abacus nimbly. The villagers all say I'm steadier at my work than a scale weight.
06553: Huang Ying is an excellent cook. The food she makes is praised for miles around. She is clever, and her warm, generous manner makes people feel at home. Day after day in the kitchen sometimes wears on her, but she sticks with it, winning everyone over with her delicious food.
06554: We don't really need a cook.
06555: We'll have good food from now on!
06556: Sect Master, my name is Huang Ying. Preparing a banquet for thirty people in three shichen is everyday work for me, and I can make something new out of leftovers too. Sometimes I do stare blankly at the stove, but as soon as I hear the villagers laughing over their meal, I'm full of energy again.
06557: Tang Tang is a girl full of curiosity about the world. She is frank and bold, doesn't fuss over small things, and can make friends with all walks of life. Through this, she joined an obscure little sect and learned some fist and kick skills. But her single-minded stubbornness often gives her master headaches, which keeps her from studying the martial arts in depth.
06559: Let's hope your fists and feet are enough for wild beasts.
06560: Sect Master, my name is Tang Tang! I learned wild boxing for three years. I can snatch a blade bare-handed, and in a fight I go for the legs and groin. Just last month I helped Aunt Wang get back her stolen grain cart. It's just... sometimes I trust the wrong people.
06561: Your artistic style doesn't suit us.
06562: From now on, the whole sect will be surrounded by your art.
06563: Sect Master, my name is Liu Yingxia. I can make twin lotuses bloom from a stubborn rock, and carve a breathing nightingale by moonlight. Of the three hundred statues in my cellar, only one has its eyes open... Would you be the first to touch it?
06564: Su Rushi showed extraordinary intelligence from childhood, with a remarkable grasp of medicines and a thorough command of pharmacology. She uses medicine skillfully on herself to sharpen her focus and keep her rest sound. Her superb medical skill and striking beauty are widely known; everyone calls her the Beautiful Doctor, and patients come one after another, hoping her skilled hands will bring them back to health.
06565: I'm not too impressed with your medical skill.
06566: May everyone be safe from now on.
06567: Sect Master, my name is Su Rushi. I can tell the cold, hot, warm and cool natures of a hundred herbs, and mix an Awakening Powder that keeps you clear-headed after three days without sleep. If anyone in the sect needs their health looked after, I'll mix the prescription that suits them best with these hands.
06568: Ban Xianglan was born a natural beauty and was once a famous courtesan in the capital. She is courteous and speaks with great finesse; every frown and smile is captivating. But she is physically frail and can't handle physical labor, which brings some helplessness to her life, yet she still gives off a charm all her own.
06569: Our sect is too small to need diplomacy.
06570: I hope you can raise our influence in the jianghu.
06571: Sect Master, my name is Ban Xianglan. At banquets in the capital I could tell apart accents from seven places, and I can get a stranger to tell me their secrets willingly in the time half an incense stick takes to burn. These hands can't hold a hoe, but they can keep every honored guest at your banquets content.
06572: Zhu Shuanghe lives nearby. He meant to make his name together with his six sworn brothers, but was separated from them by jianghu feuds, and his parents, caught up in it, have vanished. He's no fighter and owns nothing, but he has a silver tongue, talks a blue streak and is extremely good at dealing with people.
06573: Our sect takes no smooth talkers!
06574: The sect happens to be short of a good talker.
06575: Sect Master, my name is Zhu Shuanghe. I've trained a fine way with words and the art of the empty-handed thief. Out in the jianghu, whether it's negotiating and dealing with people or haggling and doing business, I'm good at it. I hope your sect will take me in!!
06576: He was sent to the Qingcheng Sect at ten and came down the mountain at twenty, having learned only one sword art in ten years. Not because he was slow, but because he felt one was enough. His master scolded him for having no ambition; he said that using one sword art for ten years without tiring of it is itself an ambition. After coming down the mountain he took a job with an escort agency. When bandits attacked an escort, he used only that one sword art, over and over, and the bandits simply couldn't find an opening; in the end they withdrew on their own.
06578: He calls himself the thirteenth-generation heir of the "Wuji Sect", and the Bone-Strengthening Pills he sells are really just rolled flour. He rotates among three towns and has never slipped up. Once he ran into someone who really knew martial arts and got three ribs broken. Once healed, he moved somewhere else and went on selling his Bone-Strengthening Pills. Someone asked if he was afraid of another beating. He said: "That guy had no martial ethics. I told him it was money back if it didn't work, and he still hit me."
06579: She is the only daughter of the Kongtong Sect Master and should have inherited his mantle, but she was expelled from the sect for talking back to an elder. She took nothing with her the day she was expelled except an old sword her master had used in his youth. Later she made a name for herself in the jianghu. People advised her to go back and apologize; the Sect Master's seat would be hers sooner or later. But she said: "Father cried when he sent me away. If I go back, he'll have cried for nothing." When these words reached Kongtong, the old Sect Master sat in the ancestral hall all night.
06580: She swept the floors of the Huashan Sect for thirty years, and no one ever noticed her. Every day she rose before dawn, swept the practice ground spotless, then sat in a corner watching the disciples practice the sword. When asked whether she knew martial arts, she shook her head: "No, I only know how to sweep." Until one year the Demonic Cult attacked the mountain and the disciples were dying or wounded; only then did she pick up her broom and, stroke by stroke, sweep every Demonic Cult master who had broken in right back out. The Sect Master knelt before her and begged her to stay. She said: "The floor's swept. Time to go."
06581: He is the most senior member of the Diancang Sect, yet he's hardly ever on the mountain, running all over the world. He likes watching the fun at markets, crouched in a corner gnawing a sesame flatbread; no one would guess he's an old fellow who has practiced the sword all his life. Asked why he doesn't stay on the mountain and enjoy himself, he says: "Up the mountain it's all rules; down the mountain it's all fun." Later, when the Diancang Sect met disaster, he rushed back overnight, took on three of the enemy's halls by himself, and when he was done, left again to go on gnawing his flatbread.
06582: He learned medicine from his mother, and she learned it from hers. He doesn't keep a clinic, but runs all over the mountains with his medicine chest on his back, staying wherever someone is sick. He takes no money if he cures them, and none if he doesn't, and leaves a few packets of herbs behind when he goes. Asked what he lives on, he says: "There are plenty of wild greens in the mountains. I won't starve." Later the villagers quietly slipped eggs and cured meat into his medicine chest; he pretended not to know, and carried it dozens of li without complaining of the weight.
06583: The eldest daughter of the Su family, with a natural allure in her eyes. Her family fell on hard times when she was young; to protect her younger sister Su Meier, she hid in the pleasure quarters and learned the arts of doubling and seduction. With her striking beauty and quick hands she dealt with every faction, until, weary of jianghu strife, she took her sister and found a sect where they could live apart from the world.
06584: Cold, beautiful and alluring, never staying in one place. She was a jianghu assassin who, unwilling to be controlled by her employers any longer, betrayed her organization in silent shoes and night-walker's clothes. Thanks to the stealth of her Dark Fox outfit she escaped her hunters many times, and after much wandering was taken in by the sect, though she still won't reveal the details of her past.
06585: She wears fox-ear hair ornaments and a fluffy tail, with a hint of allure in her cool eyes. She was once a rich family's daughter; after her family was wiped out, she was forced to learn seduction and self-defense. The fox ornaments are her mother's keepsakes: they hold her obsession, and in a fight their lively movement can bewilder an opponent. Later she found a sect, hoping to use its strength to uncover the truth of what happened to her family.
06586: Once a capable disciple of the Xiongshi Gang. Proud and unruly, he was thrown out for his showy ways and for breaking the gang's rules. His kung fu is intact; after drifting around the jianghu, he found a sect to settle in for the time being.
06587: He chopped off heads all his life, with hands as steady as iron. Before an execution he never spoke to the condemned, nor drank for courage; he just stood there, and when the hour came, the blade rose and the head fell. After retiring he opened a butcher shop, and he cuts meat the same way, one stroke, not a hair off. At first the neighbors didn't dare buy his meat; later they found he cut it more neatly than anyone, and slowly got used to it.
06588: This man steals only cattle, and only from wealthy families. He never sells them locally; he drives them dozens of li and sells them at another market. Once he was caught and had three ribs broken; once healed, he went on stealing. Asked why it has to be cattle, he says: "Cattle are valuable. One will feed me for half a year." Asked why he doesn't do something honest, he says: "Can you steal honest things?" Later the authorities, unable to do anything about him, simply turned a blind eye, since everyone he stole from was a rich family that bullied the common folk anyway.
06589: She was once the Emei Sect disciple most likely to inherit its mantle, but at twenty she packed her bags and left. No one knows why, and she doesn't say. Later someone saw her in Jiangnan running a small teahouse that sells both tea and wine. Asked if she still practices the sword, she pointed at the firewood: all fine sword-wood, which makes the tea especially fragrant. People from the Emei Sect have come looking for her; she won't go back and won't explain, only brews them a pot of tea.
06590: Every morning she carries a flower basket into the city, filled with freshly picked gardenias, jasmine and tuberoses. She doesn't call out; she just stands on the street corner and lets the scent find its own way into people's noses. Her buyers are all regulars; when they have no money, she'll take a handful of rice instead. Asked why she doesn't farm in the countryside, she says: "What you grow in a field is for eating. The flowers I grow are for looking at. People can't just eat; they need to see something pretty too."
06591: He wanders the streets all day, chasing off stray dogs for one family today, carrying things for another tomorrow. He takes no money, just a meal. He isn't very bright and talks in circles, but he has an honest heart. When people bully him, he holds no grudge and greets them with a grin the next day as usual. The neighbors look out for him, and anyone with leftovers saves them for him. One especially cold winter, he knocked on the door of a widow whose husband had just died, pushed the two steamed buns he'd been keeping in his shirt into her hands, turned and ran, fell, got up and kept running.
06592: He makes connections for people: those who want to hire a killer come to him, and so do those who want to fence stolen goods. He doesn't ask where things come from or where they're going; he just takes his cut, thirty percent. When people curse him as scum, he says: "I am scum, but I have rules. I stay out of thieves robbing thieves, I don't take jobs killing innocents for credit, and I won't touch anything that harms women or children." He has done gray business all his life and somehow never been hacked to death. Asked his secret, he says: "The greedy die fast. I just want to live."
06593: Su Dayue's younger sister, gentle and charming but with a hidden toughness. While her sister ran herself ragged protecting her, she secretly worked hard at hidden weapons and lightness skill. Once, with the cool air of her Moon Fox outfit, she disguised herself as a singing girl to sneak into the enemy camp and pass on messages. One sister in the open and one in the shadows, the two protected each other in perfect step, and in the end joined the sect together.
06594: Original name unknown. He was once a disciple of the Damo Monastery, but after years of hard practice he could not resist the temptations of the world and chose to return to lay life. He took off his kasaya and, carrying the kung fu he learned at the monastery, eventually joined the sect, keeping half a heart for Chan and half for worldly ties.
06595: Every year he goes up the mountain on Waking of Insects and stays until Grain Rain before coming down. He gathers herbs in the mountains, only those on sheer cliffs; he dares go where others don't. Asked what happens if he falls to his death, he says: "Then I'm dead. I'd be buried in the mountains either way." He sells his herbs to medicine shops in the city for whatever they'll give, never haggling over more or less. A medicine shop owner said there are only two kinds of people in this world who don't fear death: those who've had enough of living, and people like him.
06596: He has worked at the escort agency for twenty years and is still a path-crier; he never even made escort. He's in no hurry. Every day he carries the banner at the head of the convoy shouting "Make way-!" louder than anyone. Asked if he doesn't want to climb higher, he says: "A path-crier only has to shout. I don't have to worry about losing the cargo. What could be better?" Later a convoy was attacked and all the escorts ran, but he stood in the middle of the road with the banner and kept shouting. The bandits froze for a moment, then actually went around. When he got back, he went on being a path-crier and went on shouting.
06597: He keeps a stall outside the City God Temple, writing letters for people. He doesn't ask what they say; he just writes, reads it back once when he's done, and seals it when they nod. Once an old woman had him write to her son; partway through she started crying. He put down his brush and sat with her all afternoon, and took no money. The next day she came back with a basket of eggs. He wouldn't take it, but she pressed it on him: "You sat with me all afternoon. That's longer than my son has ever sat with me."
06598: He does magic tricks at the market: swallowing swords, breathing fire, pulling fish from an empty bowl, all of it. His stall draws the biggest crowd, not because his tricks are the best but because they're the slowest: he can drag one trick out for half a shichen, cracking jokes the whole time. When someone heckles that it's all fake, he nods: "Right, it's all fake. So show me something real." The heckler is left speechless. After packing up he goes to the tavern to drink, and when he can't pay, he does a trick to cover the bill.
06599: Her teahouse doesn't sell tea; it sells storytelling. She hires a storyteller for one show a day, tea is free, and there's just a donation box at the door: throw in money if you like, or don't. Asked how long she can keep it up like this, she says: "One day at a time." Later the storyteller fell ill and she took the stage herself, stumbling through a story while the audience doubled over laughing. Laughing or not, the donation box held twice as much as usual that day.
06600: She is the only woman disciple of the Hengshan Sect, and also its best fighter. She trains hard with the sword and is harder on herself. To learn the move "Returning Wind Fells the Goose", she stood at the edge of a cliff for three months and fell off seven times before mastering it on the eighth. Her fellow disciples admire her but also fear her, because she demands a lot of others too. Asked why she pushes so hard, she says: "My father said girls who learn martial arts amount to nothing. I want to show him that he's the one who amounts to nothing, not me."
06601: He hauls cargo on the docks, strong enough to do the work of two. After hauling he's in no rush to leave; he sits at the edge of the dock staring into space, sometimes for a whole shichen. Asked what he's thinking about, he says: "Nothing. Just looking at the water." Later a young man came to the docks who couldn't lift the cargo and was crying in frustration. He went over and carried it for him and took no money. When the young man tried to kowtow, he pulled him up: "I helped you because I wanted to, you kowtow because you want to. We don't owe each other anything." Then he sat back down at the edge of the dock to look at the water.
06602: He hung around outside a martial arts school for three years. He didn't become a student and didn't steal lessons, just stood at the gate watching every day. When they practiced the horse stance, he did too; when they practiced fist forms, he went home and copied them. The school's master couldn't stand it any longer and asked why he didn't come in if he wanted to learn. He said: "I can't pay the tuition." The master said he could do chores to pay it off. He said: "Working is working and learning is learning. They're two different things; they shouldn't be mixed." Later the master made an exception and took him in for free. Once he'd learned, he opened a school next door teaching poor families' children, also for free.
06603: He was once the youngest Protector of the Xueshan Sect, but for talking back to the Sect Master he was sentenced to three years facing a wall. The day the three years were up, he went straight down the mountain and never returned. He opened a small tavern beyond the passes, serving passing caravans. Asked if he hates the Sect Master, he says: "No. In those three years facing the wall I figured out everything in my life. It was worth it." Later, when the Sect Master fell gravely ill and sent for him, he went, knelt by the bed for the time an incense stick takes to burn, and went back beyond the passes.
06604: He cooked on Mount Wudang for twenty years and developed a real knack for tossing the wok. The Daoists all say his wok-tossing looks better than their sword practice: he flips it three feet high and not a drop of oil spills when it lands. Asked why he never learned the sword, he says: "A sword kills people; food keeps them alive. Keeping people alive is harder than killing them." Later, in a year of great drought when the villages below the mountain had nothing to eat, he carried his wok down, set up a shed at the village entrance and handed out porridge for a whole month.
06605: She was a disciple of the Quanzhen Sect who returned to lay life at twenty, her reason being that she "wanted to get married". And she did marry an honest man and opened a tofu shop. Asked if she was really throwing away all those years of studying the Dao, she says: "I didn't throw away the Dao. The Dao is in my heart. If it's in your heart, it's the same wherever you are." Later, when the Quanzhen Sect was in trouble, she went with the pole from her tofu mill on her shoulder, and when the fighting was over, came back to grinding tofu.
06606: She is the best fighter of her generation in the Tiejian Sect, but not the favorite. Her master says her "sword is too straight and she's too stubborn"; she can't take a detour or curry favor. She doesn't change. She practiced the same beginner's sword art for ten years, until her sword flew out like a rainbow. Her junior brothers laugh at her for being thickheaded; she says that once you truly master a sword art, no move can escape its reach. Later, at the Martial Arts Tournament, she beat every opponent with that beginner's sword art, then stepped down and kept practicing it, the same one.
06607: He joined the Cao Gang at seventeen and became a helmsman within three years. Not because his kung fu was so good, but because he knew the way. The canal has a thousand side channels; he remembers each after going through it once, and never strays when sailing at night. The old helmsmen weren't convinced and tested him; he drew the map without a single error. Asked how he trained, he said: "I herded cattle as a kid and walked every path in the mountains. Water paths are just like mountain ones; remember their features and that's it."
06608: He has been a night watchman for two years; he's young and quick on his feet, and never tires of walking the streets at night. He doesn't just call the hour; he calls the weather too, adding to "dry weather, beware of fire" a line like "rain tomorrow, remember to bring in your washing". Asked how he knows it'll rain tomorrow, he says: "My knees hurt." Later the neighbors trusted him more than the weather forecast. He never slacks on his rounds and patrols carefully, saying the quiet night is perfect for thinking. Asked what he thinks about, he says: "What to eat tomorrow."
06609: He worked at the smithy for three years and still could only work the bellows. His master called him a blockhead; he didn't say a word and kept pumping. Once the master fell ill and no one was doing the work; he picked up the hammer, and the master looked at what he made for a long time without speaking. Later the master asked when he had learned. He said: "I watched while you worked. Watched for three years." The master passed the shop on to him, and after taking it over he still pumped the bellows every day.
06610: He performs at the market, doing a set of fist and kick moves handed down in his family, and collects coppers after each round. His kung fu isn't great, but he's quick with his tongue and could talk the dead back to life. When people laugh that it's all show, he doesn't mind. After packing up he goes to the tavern to drink, and when he's had too much he crouches by the river staring into space. Asked what he's staring at, he says: "Thinking of my dad. He performed like this back then too. I wonder who he thought about when he stared into space."
06611: She is the Beggar Sect's only woman six-pouch disciple, and she didn't get there by seniority but by fighting. In three years in the Beggar Sect she challenged thirty-seven senior brothers and beat them all. When the Chief asked why she fights so well, she said: "I used to slaughter pigs. I know where to put the knife for the least effort." The gang later summed up a lesson: it's fine if Mochou loses her temper, but whatever you do, don't provoke her while she's holding a knife.
06612: She comes from a side branch of the Tang Sect and couldn't learn its core hidden-weapon skills, only the surface. She worked things out herself, combining hidden weapons with embroidery needles until she mastered the art of "needles hidden in embroidery". The main Tang family looks down on her, and she doesn't care. Later she opened an embroidery shop: embroidery in the open, a few jianghu jobs on the side. Once, when the Tang Sect met disaster, the main family came begging for her help; without a word she closed the shop and went with them.
06613: A disciple of an unknown jianghu sect who escaped a great calamity that shook the jianghu, and came together with a group of people met while fleeing to plan how to survive this spreading disaster.
06614: Not a traditional martial artist, but a genius with bows, crossbows, hidden weapons and mechanisms. He has worn a mask for years, moving between shadow and forest, and is the deadliest ranged fighter in sect battles.
06615: In his youth he was a down-and-out scholar who, having seen through the rise and fall of the world, turned to seeking the Dao. Watching a flying crane fight a black snake, he grasped the true meaning of "softness overcomes hardness". He has no taste for killing, and most of his moves dissolve and redirect, but if someone crosses his line, the push-hands of the Taiji Divine Skill can shatter the life meridians of every living thing within ten zhang.
06617: A lone swordsman who pursues "no move beats every move". He is solitary by nature; apart from the sword, nothing in the world catches his eye. He moves like the wind, often sheathing his sword before his opponent has even noticed.
06618: The mightiest Protector of the Buddhist order, wearing a ragged kasaya yet with an indestructible vajra body. He is upright and blunt, responsible for putting down traitors within the sect and demons from outside. He was once a god of slaughter on the battlefield, and became a monk out of remorse.
06620: A dashing young gentleman in a splendid blue robe, versed in the martial arts of a hundred schools and especially good at "using the enemy's force against them". His sect is known for gathering the best of all schools, and is the most mysterious intelligence center in the jianghu.
06621: Legend says he sat for three years on the ice plains of the far north, watching glaciers crack and listening to the thunder, and grasped the Three Return to One. He can turn his qi into extreme cold to freeze opponents, and can even call down heavenly thunder. As a representative of the highest powers, no one has ever survived his fists; he is the summit every disciple both reveres and fears.

07099: Reporting, Young Sect Master: I've just surveyed the land. There's plenty of water nearby, the ground is level, it's easy to defend and hard to attack, and good for hunting. This place can serve as our temporary home.
07100: Very good. This past month, everyone has followed me hiding here and there, fleeing from Wangyue Peak to this wild valley. You've all been through so much!
07101: Don't say that, Young Sect Master! As long as I still have breath, this hardship is nothing. We'll fight our way back for sure!
07102: Taking back Wangyue Peak isn't empty talk. First we have to survive in this wilderness and gain a foothold.
07103: Yes, Young Sect Master! No, Sect Master!
07104: I may not be fit to be Sect Master yet, but one day we will take it all back and restore the sect!
07105: First let's see what resources around here can keep us alive, gather a few, then find a way to fill our bellies!
07106: Yes, I'll see to it right away!
07107: We need to get to know this land first.
07108: See this wooden tablet in front of you? Channel your internal energy along its patterns, think of the directions in your mind, and try moving forward, back, left and right. This is the [Position-Sensing Formula] my father taught me; now it's just right for surveying the land.
07109: (Delighted) Sect Master, this method makes the body move so nimbly!
07110: {T1}Send someone to check the {/T}{T2}carriage{/T}{T3} to the east. We came here in such a hurry that our supplies were destroyed; see if anything useful can be found. Remember to move with the steps I just showed you and don't disturb the wild beasts.{/T}
07112: Sect Master, there's cloth and wound medicine in the carriage, and some dry rations too!
07113: Looks like things aren't so bad. We need to store these supplies properly, especially the food. Left out in the wind and sun, it may spoil before long.
07114: {T1}Go cut down those tall {/T}{T2}trees{/T}{T3}, and gather some of the low {/T}{T4}shrubs{/T}{T5}. We'll need them for building houses. Use a deft touch when cutting, and don't get hurt by the thorns.{/T}
07115: Thank you for the reminder, Sect Master!
07116: That should be enough for now.
07117: {T1}First build some {/T}{T2}shacks{/T}{T3}. Things keep longer under a roof, our {/T}{T4}hay beds{/T}{T5} can go under the shacks too, and everyone will have somewhere to shelter from wind and rain for now.{/T}
07118: {T1}Then build a few {/T}{T2}warehouses{/T}{T3} to store these supplies.{/T}
07119: Sect Master, how does it look? I'm out of practice and built it a bit slowly, but at least we won't get rained on tonight!
07120: {T1}Not bad, it's starting to take shape! The nights are cold, so light a {/T}{T2}bonfire{/T}{T3} too. A {/T}{T4}bonfire{/T}{T5} doesn't just keep us warm; we can cook on it too.{/T}
07121: {T1}Watch how high the clay pot hangs over the fire: too low and it burns, too high and it won't cook. Use the {/T}{T2}bonfire{/T}{T3} to make some {/T}{T4}braised flatbread{/T}{T5} to fill everyone's stomachs.{/T}
07122: Aha, now this feels like home!
07123: The nights are cold, so light a bonfire too. A bonfire doesn't just keep us warm; we can cook on it too.
07124: Watch how high the clay pot hangs over the fire: too low and it burns, too high and it won't cook. Use the bonfire to make some braised flatbread to restore everyone's strength.
07125: Sect Master, this braised flatbread warms me right through.
07126: So, we've more or less settled in.
07127: {T1}I thought about it all night: we need to restore the sect's crafts as soon as possible! The sect's tech must not die out with me. Copy out these {/T}{T2}building methods{/T}{T3} and see if we can restore some of the sect's tech.{/T}
07128: {T1}Yes, Sect Master. I grew up in the mountains and know a bit of {/T}{T2}farming{/T}{T3}; I'll write it into these building methods to record the sect's tech.{/T}
07129: Very good. If we can read the soil and grow crops, at least we won't go hungry.
07130: Sect Master, it's done. While writing, I looked at the soil here. We can start by planting some wheat and cotton: wheat to fill our bellies, cotton to weave cloth and make clothes. What do you think, Sect Master?
07131: Good! Then let's sow the seeds of hope.
07132: Now we just have to wait a while, and there'll be a harvest!
07133: But while surveying the area, I found a plant by the ridges of the field to the west that seems possible to cultivate. Send careful disciples to take turns observing it and recording how it grows, so in the future we can grow it for our own use.
07134: I'll arrange it now and record everything carefully, and won't miss the slightest change!
07135: It looks like it will be quite a lot of trouble to cultivate this plant, and everyone's been struggling with gathering and chopping these past days. We don't seem to have proper tools.
07136: In the old days, the Armory Pavilion that Hall Master Feng ran in our sect had some books on woodworking. We should have brought them out with us. Go see whether we can make some tools.
07137: {T1}Yes, Sect Master. Then I'll build a {/T}{T2}Handcraft Bench{/T}{T3} first. It can make all kinds of wooden tools, and from then on, repairs and building will take half the effort.{/T}
07138: But with everyone out laboring together, other areas seem short-handed. We should let the disciples who know farming best look after the fields, and let the other disciples do the work they're better at first!
07139: Yes, as you command, Sect Master.
07140: Sect Master, that's a very sensible arrangement. With everyone's tasks clear, we won't be scrambling like before. Efficiency is bound to go up a lot.
07141: Work is arranged; now we need to set a daily schedule too.
07142: Rise at dawn to practice boxing and build strength, start work in the morning, rest a little at noon to recover, go over the day's affairs at dusk, and go to bed in the late evening. Only a regular routine lets everyone build up their strength.
07143: This stone is very unusual. It's just like the curious stones in the sect's Treasure Pavilion!
07144: Sect Master, everyone seems more energetic and in a better mood!
07145: But none of you must let play sap your will. Just now, looking into the distance, I saw what seem to be bandits and petty thieves roaming not far from here. We may have escaped the fighting, but this place isn't exactly peaceful! We need some proper weapons.
07146: I'll see to it right away!
07147: Once the weapons are made, everyone can hunt some game nearby for practice so their skills don't get rusty. Remember to butcher the game on the spot so it stays fresh.
07148: Sect Master, we did it! Look...
07149: Very good! What's wrong with you? Why are you limping?
07150: It's nothing. A deer's hoof just scraped me while I was butchering it. It's fine!
07151: Put the venison down at once! How can you say it's fine? If a leg wound spreads, that's no small matter. Hurry, go prepare some wound medicine, and don't be careless! I'll protect the qi and blood around the wound with the Qingyun Method!
07154: Thank you for your concern, Sect Master. We're all fine!
07155: Good! They dare come here with such clumsy kung fu? One day we'll round them all up in one go!
07156: But this time they seemed to be only testing us. We need to build some defenses quickly in case they come again.
07157: If I understand you, Sect Master, we can build wooden houses with beams, pillars, doors, windows and eaves? That's far grander than shacks. It'll be so comfortable to live in! Ah, that hurts...
07158: Sect Master! With all this, we'll send them packing in defeat!
07159: Don't celebrate too soon. When we fought them off, everyone's martial skills seemed rusty. Our top priority is to train quickly and grow stronger!
07160: Yes, Sect Master. But we left in such a hurry that the martial manuals were all left behind.
07161: Hmm... Let's first see what we have on hand, then look around nearby for anything else.
07162: Everyone has been working day and night clearing land and building these past days. Many are starting to look tired; if this goes on, I'm afraid they'll grow weary and start slacking.
07163: You notice everything, Sect Master! Some disciples have indeed said privately that at night there's nothing to do but tend wounds and sit in meditation, and it gets dull after a while.
07164: Our sect was once quite accomplished with curios and curious stones. We can build some things for the disciples to admire and enjoy, to lift their spirits.
07165: Sect Master! While hunting I ran into a gang of bandits by accident. They seem to have had their eye on us since we entered the valley!
07166: Hmph! We haven't sunk so low that petty thieves like you can push us around! Disciples, hear my order: take your positions and follow me against the enemy!
07167: Sect Master, I'm much better. Sorry to have worried you!
07168: Treating wounds is only a stopgap. To hold off enemies for good, we need a solid foundation!
07169: We need to open our Dantians and train in martial arts as soon as possible. Only then can we hold off enemies and protect ourselves.
07170: You're right, Sect Master, but I don't know where to start. The bandits withdrew today, but there's no telling that stronger enemies won't come later.
07171: As our sect's books say: calm the mind and still the breath, draw qi into the body, and strike at the Dantian!
07172: Steady your mind, don't rush! Guide the qi with your intent, open up the meridians, and the Dantian will open!
07173: (Internal energy flowing, looking delighted) Sect Master! I've learned how to open the Dantian! When I circulate it, my whole body feels full of internal energy. If enemies come again, I can fight back!
07174: Our Dantians are open; we've earned the right to stand our ground here. Now there's only one last step: raise our Sect Gate and set our name right!
07176: {T1}I'm afraid we can't use the old name "Tianji Sect" anymore. The Xueying Cult is still searching for us everywhere, and the old name would draw attention. Let's choose a {/T}{T2}new name{/T}{T3} for our new sect!{/T}
07177: This is a great matter for the sect. It's entirely your decision, Sect Master!
07178: {T1}A new sect needs to bring in talent from everywhere. Sect affairs are growing lately, and you handle things reliably. From now on you will be {/T}{T2}Inner Hall Master{/T}{T3}, helping with recruiting disciples and day-to-day arrangements.{/T}
07179: Thank you for your trust, Sect Master! I'll give it my all and won't let the slightest thing go wrong in the sect's affairs!

08815: Xiao Shitou, one of our outer disciples, is marrying the daughter of the tofu shop down the mountain. His fellow disciples have pooled money for gifts but are still a few things short. Please gather the list and deliver it before the deadline, so the couple can have a proper wedding.

08818: This year marks a hundred years since our founder's passing, and every branch hall is coming back to the mountain to pay respects, so we need far more than in past years. 08823: Our Sect Master's beloved daughter is marrying into a renowned orthodox sect, and this match ties our two sects together for decades to come. Not one item of the dowry can look shabby, so this shipment must arrive in full. We hope your sect will do all it can to help.

08826: The night before last, Heifeng Stronghold bandits came down the mountain, burned Liu Village to the ground, took the grain and livestock, and carried off several young men. The stronghold can only be stormed once, so it must succeed in one go.

13357: A distant melody comes from deep in the gorge, its echoes lingering between the rock walls. With the sect newly founded, heaven and earth feel especially vast.
13358: The canyon wind turns an untitled page of music. Collected after founding a sect at Juechen Valley.
13360: A bright line skims over high walkways and dangerous paths with the rhythm of a journey far away. The deep gorge gains a little human warmth.
13361: The melody still waits beyond the cloud walkway. Collected once the Juechen Valley sect reaches level 3.
13363: A slow, heavy music flows into the ravines like echoes returning from distant mountains. The sect's foundation is set, and even this remote place has a home.
13364: The ravines haven't yet sent back the full echo. Collected once the Juechen Valley sect reaches level 5.
13366: A low rhythm rises and falls with the tide, like oars first knocking on the southern shore. The new sect slowly takes shape among the wind and waves.
13367: The sound of the tide drowns out an untitled page of music. Collected after founding a sect at the Nanhai Islands.
13369: Lively rhythms weave with foreign tones, like a boat passing through a faraway harbor. The sea wind brings unfamiliar roads and new bustle.
13370: The sea wind hasn't yet blown open the rolled-up page. Collected once the Nanhai Islands sect reaches level 3.
13372: A broad soundscape and strong beat spread over the sea together, the islands seeming to resonate with the tide. By now the sect is enough for sailors to know its lights.
13373: The islands still wait for the same tide. Collected once the Nanhai Islands sect reaches level 5.
13375: Once all nine tunes from the three places are collected, a low melody that belongs to no mountain, gorge or island sounds from between the pages. Strange and faint, it seems to point to a world beyond the sect yet unseen.

13379: A page of music sealed in lingering winter. Its music can only be made out after collecting all 9 tunes from the three places.
13381: From Fengsha. Bright rhythms and layered melodies answer each other, like people's steps keeping pace during midsummer work. With everyone pulling together, the busyness becomes a rousing, joyful song.
13382: A page of music hidden among the noise of midsummer. Its ensemble can only be heard clearly after collecting all 9 tunes from the three places.
