13616: Lets you plant wheat. From wild grass to ears of wheat, our ancestors' craft can't be lost! You can also cook a hot pot of grain porridge, so at least you won't starve. Eating your fill will take a bit more figuring out, of course.
13618: Learn to make the Handcraft Bench. Using wood to work wood: human wisdom is just that plain! Farewell to the primitive craft of gnawing wood with your teeth. Of course, the odds of your hand slipping and shaving a finger have gone up too.
13620: The millstone creaks round and the heap of grain turns to snowy flour in a moment. A small Star Energy flame leaps onto the iron griddle, fragrance rises, and the first hot flatbread comes out, golden and crisp, like the harvest kneaded into the morning breeze.
13622: Learn to build the {T1}Drying Rack{/T}, used to make {T2}jerky{/T} and {T3}dried fruit{/T}.
13624: The fresh scent of logs spreads along the data patterns, fences rise from the ground, shelves stand against the walls and wall lamps hang down soft palace light. The disciple quarters become a breathing little wooden universe in an instant.
13626: Learning to build houses is your first step to putting down roots in the wild. It lets you keep off the rain with a Large Shack, train at a Stone Arena and sit around the fire at outdoor stone tables and stools. From sleeping rough to having a "home" where you can rest, train and gather.
13629: Learn to build {T1}Courtyard Walls{/T}, {T2}Courtyard Gates{/T} and {T3}Basic House{/T} blueprints.
13632: Learn to use {T1}[Bluestone Bricks]{/T} for house structure parts.
13634: Learn to make a stove. Three stones and a pot: the smoke makes your eyes stream, but at least you get hot food! You'll often misjudge the heat and fry things to charcoal, but at least you won't starve!
13636: Starlight falls along the guide, a well wells up from the ground, firewood stacks itself against the wall, and poplar seeds sprout in the soft light, painting the space outside the quarters into a breathing meadow in an instant.
13638: Star patterns light up along the wood grain, and wooden beds, oil lamps, wardrobes and palace lanterns unlock one by one, as if inviting the moonlight and pine wind of a thousand years ago into the room.
13640: Star patterns sweep the eaves and walls, and storage chests and small screens quietly unlock. Chests hold the clutter and screens shut out the noise, and the room's fresh log scent can breathe freely.
13642: Learn to build the {T1}Sandbag{/T}, a place for disciples to train fist-type combat moves.
13644: Unlocks the dining hall and its tables, chairs and benches, so disciples can finally enjoy a good meal!
13646: The courtyard comes alive like a moving spring painting: the wind from the swing tosses laughter to the eaves, and the double bed whispers behind its gauze curtain, inviting the starlight to sleep.
13649: A qin stand: pluck the seven strings lightly and all sounds fall still. An ancient sword statue stands quietly, its edge sheathed, reflecting a clear heart. From now on, martial training starts with silence; listening to wind and rain, every sound is one sword, one heart.
13650: Learn to build {T1}Ponds{/T}, so you can build ponds in the sect to decorate the surroundings.
13653: Unlocks a range of aquatic plants to decorate ponds, lay out the sect and beautify the surroundings.
13655: Unlocks a range of water buildings to decorate ponds, lay out the sect and beautify the surroundings.
13657: Unlocks covered water bridges: combine covered bridge and arch bridge parts into a covered bridge over water, for decoration or for disciples to cross.
13659: Learn to roast tea. Fermented tea leaves turn as red as fire! Greens, radish and old cured pork stewed in one pot with tea: you've unlocked the ultimate farmhouse survival dish, the big pot stew. As for how it looks...
13661: Star patterns tremble on the drum, and bamboo-shadow, dark-leaf and stone-grain walls open together. In a moment the wind knocks green snow, dark tides surge at night and cold stone hums low, and the quiet room becomes an autumn ode you can hear and see.
13663: Can make fine dishes. The disciples have unlocked seasoning skills. Chefs at this level often argue over whether tofu pudding should be sweet or savory, but they all agree mapo tofu should be numbing.
13665: Learn to farm paddy fields and grow rice. Golden waves roll when the wind blows, terraces are cut into the hills, and planting skills improve. A drunk disciple falling into the field counts as extra fertilizer.
13667: Bluestone steps spread out at a word, the sect gate raises its eaves and pillars, star patterns are carved across the archway, guide stones wind along the lamps, and the welcome pavilion gathers the first light of day. From now on the gate divides the immortal from the mortal; one step outside is the jianghu.
13669: The Peony Flowerbed blooms and fades in silence, teaching you to keep your true heart amid splendor. The Ornamental Pagoda Tree scatters shadows in the wind, reminding you to breathe deeply under every patch of shade. From now on, martial training starts with the heart; heaven and earth open wide and the spirit comes home.
13672: The post station flag snaps in the wind, the pigeon loft circles on star tracks, and supply packs drop out of thin air. In an instant hooves, wings and streams of resources arrive together, and the sect's lifeblood connects to the outside world.
13674: Cloud-Shadow Moon Lamps rise first, their light like thin cloud over the moon. A long curio bookshelf stands against the wall, scrolls lined up with stardust. A luohan bed spreads its low screen; lie down and the room's wood scent and lamplight slowly merge into a night boat.
13675: Unlocks the {T1}Shuttle Platform{/T}, which lets you travel quickly across the world at a steep price.
13678: Learn stone building structures. Deep foundations plus stone-brick reinforcement double building durability! Carved stone tables and stools look nicer too; they just burn your backside in summer and chill your bones in winter.
13680: Reading desks, copying desks and writing desks line up in a star-patterned book array, and the two small ornaments, idle books and a brush rack, shimmer with light and ink. The paper-scented room becomes a whispering sea of stars you can write and read.
13682: Can make even finer dishes. The disciples have learned wok-tossing and other advanced techniques. Tasty or not, it looks good while they cook.
13684: Learn a basic internal art method. Draw the qi of heaven and earth into the body! At first all you can manage is a fart, but at least it counts as "internal energy".
13686: Unlocks the basic Wooden Dummy. The disciples finally don't have to beat each other up to train. It's just that the clanging gives the Sect Master a headache...
13688: Includes facilities for holding, punishing and executing prisoners, a full one-stop service. We'll make sure they feel right at home!
13689: Cold light cracks across the Sword-Testing Stone, the Armored Mannequin holds its weapon waiting to be cut, the Zhenwu Demon-Quelling Painting hangs on the wall to ward off evil, and Longquan's cold gleam leaves its sheath and goes onto the rack. Star patterns hum low in the room with the wind of the blades, and the air of killing grows almost solid.
13691: The Chinese Rose Flowerbed is in bud month after month, writing the years in undying cinnabar. The Ornamental Pine stands tall, making wind and snow bow and keeping you evergreen. From now on, even the wilds have blades and poetry; flowers that never fade, a spirit that endures.
13695: Unlocks the Basic Camp tech, so no more sleeping rough! Torches light the night, the Furnace smelts the first iron, bricks and stones raise walls against wind and rain, and a big stove makes meals tastier. The sect's home starts right here!
13697: Star Energy collection is go! The Moonlight Platform absorbs the essence of the moon, the Thousand Stars Energy Cauldron gathers starlight, the Star-Gathering Tube catches stardust and the Star Energy Storage Pool stores power. Your advanced sect starts here, and ruling the jianghu is only a matter of time!
13698: The smithy is open! The Smithing Bench rings away, silver-inlaid leather tools make a shiny debut, one wave of the Command Flag looks mighty, and the brazier is toasty warm. From now on disciples leave handwork behind and enjoy upgraded gear!
13700: Iron Refining unlocked! Sparks fly in the Refining Furnace, pig iron ingots become fine iron ingots, and the Moon-Lit Lantern shines bright. Better metal means advanced gear is no longer a dream, and the sect's fighting power shoots up!
13702: Precious Metalwork! Gold and silver ingots gleam, gold-inlaid leather tool kits look classy, and quarrying techniques bring the resources rolling in. The sect will never be short of money again, and the disciples' gear shines gold!
13705: Star Energy Use unlocked! Conduction towers carry power, the Star Energy Mill never stops turning, and Star Energy Hanging Lamps make night bright as day. Star Energy is no longer just for show; it's a strong driving force for the sect's growth, boosting both life and production!
13707: Climate Control is online! The Star Energy Heater warms the winter, the Star Energy Cooler cools the summer and Star Energy food storage keeps food fresh for longer. The disciples won't suffer the weather anymore, and the sect is like spring all year round!
13709: Basic Weaving unlocked! The Loom creaks away, tier 1 cloth keeps coming, beast accessories add personality, and one wave of the Commander's Banner fills everyone with spirit. Disciples no longer go about half-dressed, and the sect's image improves at once!
13711: Weaponry Lv 1 unlocked! The Parting Sorrow Sword shows its edge, the Sky-Breaker Bow hits the mark at a hundred paces, the Luchen Spear sweeps all before it and the Bedrock Gauntlets pack enormous force. Disciples now have weapons to defend themselves, and the sect is safer
13713: Weaponry Lv 2 unlocked! The strategy sand table plans every move, the Mechanism Bench runs with precision, Mechanism Cores surge with power, the plain porcelain bearing turns smoothly and the Ink Crystal Pillar is full of energy. The sect's mechanism arts reach a new level, and its strategic planning is a cut above!
13715: Mechanism Applications unlocked! Mechanical men work without complaint, their charging posts top up their energy at any time, and the mechanical man schematic "All-Round" doubles their abilities. The sect now has a crowd of tireless helpers, and production shoots up!
13717: Star Energy Weaponry unlocked! The Star Energy Smithing Bench radiates power, the Tiger Bone Gauntlets could lift mountains, refined metal tools are razor-sharp, and the Clear River Sword and Green Frost Bow are unstoppable. A perfect blend of Star Energy and weapons sends the disciples' fighting power off the charts!
13719: Ranged Mechanisms unlocked! Mechanical Crossbows rain bolts, Mechanism Cores pack strong power, mechanical birds soar through the sky and breed in their nests, and the Reed Leaf Spear shows its edge. The sect's ranged strike power rises sharply; enemies are beaten before they get close!
13721: Advanced Mechanisms unlocked! Mechanical birds speed up like lightning and carry twice the load, and mechanical men learn to craft. The sect's mechanism arts reach their peak and its tech leads all rivals!
13724: Livestock Facilities unlocked! Tamed animals become able helpers, animal hay beds are as cozy as home, wooden feeding troughs are full to the brim, and there's plenty of herbivore and carnivore feed. The sect's livestock thrives, with plenty of meat, eggs and milk!
13726: Simple Accessories unlocked! The Bamboo Frame Pack holds your things, Bamboo Slips record wisdom, the long staff is good for self-defense and fitness, and the Rattle Drum adds some fun. The disciples' gear is more complete!
13728: Leathercraft unlocked! The Sewing Table hums, Straw Sandals are comfy and hard-wearing, cotton long coats and trousers are warm and practical, and the wardrobe keeps things tidy. Disciples say goodbye to rags, and their quality of life shoots up!
13730: Medicine Making unlocked! 14308: Builders' Guild reminder: building training halls taller than three floors is strictly forbidden, to avoid flight accidents involving high-ranking sects.
14309: Strange news! A "glowing divine stone" appeared on the southern mountain, drawing hundreds of heroes to watch all night. It turned out to be a luminous pearl dropped by a drunk swordsman.
14310: Formal statement: the "Nine Yin Scripture: Crash Course" recently on the market is actually a mix-up of Nine Yin White Bone Claw and a Mapo Tofu Recipe Book. Fellow Daoists, please don't buy it.
14311: A great sect's "Blindfolded Sword Flying" contest flew into geese migrating south and was turned into a charity "Pick Up the Feathers" event.
14312: Complaints desk: Widow Wang of a certain village protests that with so many sects nearby, the "Ha! Hey!" every morning is seriously disrupting her hens' laying.
14313: Trend watch: "ripped-style" Daoist robes are in this year. It's said the higher a master's training progress, the more patches on their clothes.
14314: Anti-scam weekly: beware of recruitment ads promising "guaranteed placement, a free spirit beast and a free Dao companion". There's no free lunch in the jianghu, only free beatings.
14315: Experts debunk: the shrieks from the back mountains at midnight aren't ghosts, just a certain Sect Master venting after a failed training session. Nearby residents can rest easy.
14316: Hermits long in seclusion, the "sweeping monks" and "old fishermen", are returning to the jianghu one after another, muttering that they want to see this prodigy who rewrote the rankings.
14317: The rare qilin of the deep mountains and marshes has been sighted often lately. Someone even saw it as tame as a dog outside the forbidden grounds of a top sect, apparently subdued by some supreme divine art.
14318: The Imperial Observatory, watching the stars at night, saw a new star blazing beside the Ziwei Star, as if about to swallow the heavens. The divination reads: "A sect rises; the martial world changes hands."
14319: A painter from the capital sat at the foot of your sect's mountain for seven days and nights for a glimpse of the strongest Sect Master of the age, finally producing A Spirit to Swallow Mountains and Rivers. Copies are sold out all over Luoyang.
14320: A fine weapon doesn't have to be sharpened every day, but it must be polished every day. Not for sharpness: in a duel, the cold glint of sunlight off the blade can blind your opponent and win you a precious 0.5 seconds to strike.
14321: Never look down on beggars by the road. They have the best gossip in town and are the biggest "intelligence relay" in the jianghu. Whether you give a bowl of meat or a bone decides if tomorrow you're known as "a paragon of honor" or "an utter miser".
14322: Don't panic if you fall off a cliff. By jianghu logic, there's always a cave at the bottom, always a skeleton in the cave, and always a secret manual beside the skeleton. If you found nothing, you fell the wrong way. Try climbing up again.
14323: The one who walks into the inn shouting "a thousand cups and I won't get drunk" usually goes down after three bowls, while the one sipping plain water in the corner can drink you into an existential crisis. In the jianghu, restraint is the highest form of swagger.
14324: Hidden weapons are all about surprise, but righteous sects usually shout a token "Dart!" before throwing. If you meet an opponent who starts scattering hidden weapons without a word, run. That's a professional killer with no martial ethics.
14325: If the inn's bun filling is unusually tasty and chewy but there isn't a pig within ten li, put down your chopsticks and politely ask the landlady: this meat... what was its name in life?
14326: A hero carrying an umbrella on a sunny day usually has a sword, a mechanism or poison smoke hidden in it. Likewise, someone carrying an erhu isn't always a musician; they might be a madman who kills with sound waves. Jianghu instruments: killing first, music second.
14327: All hail the Supreme of the Martial World! Sect Master, now that you sit firmly in place {%s}, the jianghu is no longer a wild land of rival heroes but your own palace. From a crumbling shack of a few bricks and tiles to today's dazzling everlasting legacy, you carved open a new age with the sword in your hand and the spirit in your chest. Now one letter from you can end a frontier war and one look can bring a fiend lord to justice. Place {%s}: who else in this world deserves it but you?
14328: Congratulations on truly reaching the top, Sect Master! Place {%s}, and behind that number lie the shattered dreams of countless challengers. Your name is now the jianghu's most expensive taboo; the so-called righteous sects bathe and burn incense before they even mention it. Once you pressed on through the mud; now you look down on all beings from the clouds. From now on the rules of the jianghu are yours to set on a whim. Even if you said crows were white, every painter in the martial world would rush out to buy white paint.
14329: Quite right, Sect Master! In place {%s}, you've gone beyond "martial arts" into something like a natural disaster or a miracle. Our editors have worn out the old books these past days and still can't find the words to praise your feats. Call your moves exquisite? That insults your divine footwork. Call your foundation deep? That belittles your talent. In the end, the Jianghu Gazette may have to print nothing but your portrait, because any words look pale and feeble before place {%s}.
14330: Sect Master, this is "when one person attains the Dao, even their chickens and dogs rise to heaven" come true. Looking at place {%s}, I can't help remembering the days you hauled bricks with a few scrawny disciples. Now if you spit, they'll enshrine it as immortal dew. The jianghu has gone completely mad, but it has also completely submitted. In the shadow of place {%s}, every ambition has become flattery and every struggle obedience. You are the jianghu's final answer.
14331: What is a king's might? This! No blade or sword needed; one "I don't like it" turns the bloody jianghu into a paradise of song and dance. Sect Master, the name of place {%s} works a hundred times better than an official wanted poster. The youngsters who once shouted about challenging you are now busy copying your calligraphy. In this jianghu you're the only sun; the other stars either hide in the clouds or live off your light.
14332: Sect Master, that's not martial training, that's redecorating the planet! In place {%s}, your output alone equals the whole jianghu's. Nobody cares who has mastered some peerless divine art anymore; everyone only cares whether you'll plant new vegetables in the back mountains tomorrow so they can catch a whiff. Growing a sect to this size, you're not just number one in the martial world, you're the greatest money manager and infrastructure fiend of all time.
14333: Ah, the loneliness of the invincible. Sect Master, you've raised the ceiling of martial arts so high that later generations won't even dare dream of it. People used to fight over rankings; now they only fight over who kneels most properly before you. The view from place {%s} is glorious, but it really is a bit lonely. Why not go easy one day and deliberately lose a move to a stray cat, to give these despairing jianghu folk a little false hope?
14334: Your Eminence, even the immortals can't sit still! The name of place {%s} has stirred heaven itself. But if you ask me, what's so great about the immortal realm? There you'd have to start over as a new disciple, while here in the jianghu your word is law. I suggest you keep that envoy here to sweep the sect's floors and teach everyone how to grow immortal elixirs on the side. After all, it's only the jianghu while you're in this mortal world; if you left, I wouldn't even have the motivation to write this paper.
14335: This is the last spicy review we'll write for you, Sect Master. From 99th to place {%s}, we've witnessed the birth of a legend. You need no ranking to vouch for you now; wherever you stand is the center of the martial world, and your will is where the jianghu ends. Thank you for giving us scribblers the most magnificent ending. In the years to come, please keep ruling this undying land as place {%s}!
14336: The Ministry of War has just issued a new order: since disciples of the top-ranked sect cause traffic gridlock just going down the mountain to buy vegetables, the capital's constables are tripled. Their only duty: keep the screaming crowds in order when the top sect goes out, and prevent stampedes.
14337: The Minister of Revenue is deeply worried: the top sect's presence is so overwhelming that folk say "better offend the Emperor than anger the top Sect Master". Gold death-pardon tablets, once priceless, have crashed on the black market; two of them won't buy one "auditor's pass" to the top sect.
14338: The Ministry of Rites is urgently discussing whether to make several single core disciples of the top sect princes of a different surname and send seventeen princesses up the mountain for a "cultural exchange". The Emperor's note: We'd like to go too, but We can't leave the realm.
14339: So heroes across the land can rush overnight to queue at the foot of the top sect's mountain to "breathe qi", the court has officially lifted the curfew in every prefecture along the way. The reason: as long as that Sect Master is around, the realm is quieter than a morgue.
14340: New Ministry of Personnel review rules: any local official seeking promotion must submit a "group portrait" or "correspondence" with a steward of the top sect. Anyone who can prove they once sent bricks to that sect will be first in line for military governor.
14341: The holder of the "Sky-Piercing Needle", ranked 999th on the weapon list, announced their retirement yesterday. The reason: the embroidery needle is so small it fell in the river while they were doing laundry and they couldn't find it.
14342: The capital's yamen has received many complaints about young heroes who, trying to look cool, climbed the city wall and got caught on the gate studs. The city guards sigh: heroes, please use the gate like everyone else. We're not responsible for picking anyone off the studs.
14343: The Yuelai Inn hereby declares: "table-shattering" internal energy contests are banned on the premises. Offenders will pay for the furniture and stay to wash dishes for three months. Six Sect Masters are currently scrubbing away in the back kitchen.
14344: A manual titled Learn the Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms in Three Days has turned up on the street, priced at two coins. Page one says "first, find a dragon"; page two says "hit it eighteen times". The buyer says: the logic is airtight.
14345: The authorities have set up "demon-revealing mirrors" on the post roads. A saber fighter from the Western Regions rode so fast his wig blew off and badly blocked the view of the donkey cart behind him. His horse fodder was confiscated for three days.
14346: Two swordsmen in Jiangnan agreed to duel on a bridge and faced off for three days and nights without drawing. Just as everyone thought they were contesting internal energy, one of them spoke: "Brother, my leg's cramping. Could you give me a hand?"
14347: Lately some heroes have been feeding dragon fruit to a spirit rabbit in the mountains, turning its fur red. Passersby mistook it for a "baby fire qilin", sparking a mass hunt. The spirit rabbit says: I just want to eat grass in peace.
14348: Tang Sect disciples have developed a new hidden weapon, the "Nag". It doesn't hurt when it hits, but it plays "your martial arts are trash" in your ear on a random loop for three hours. Victims report: low physical damage, huge psychological scars.
14349: A new business called "proxy horse stance" has appeared in the jianghu: pay up and someone will squat in the sect square for you. A puzzled elder asks: why do this year's disciples all have wasted leg muscles after three years in the sect?
14350: The Beggar Sect has launched a "Dragon-Subduing Delivery" service, promising delivery within one incense stick or the meal is free. The biggest problem so far: couriers keep meeting old enemies on the road and dueling, spilling the food everywhere.
14351: Jueqing Valley announces a change of business: no more heartbreak grass, it's growing napa cabbage now. The Valley Master sighs: jianghu grudges don't fill your belly. Isn't cabbage stir-fried with pork delicious?
14352: The Jianghu Mediation Committee appeals: heroes, please show some restraint when naming moves. Yesterday someone shouted "Heaven-Devouring Earth-Destroying Limitless Supreme Slash" and only clipped their opponent's nails. It was extremely awkward.
14353: A master who lived thirty years in seclusion came down the mountain to find the world had changed. He meant to light a fire with internal energy, but a passerby handed him a fire starter: "Don't bother, old man. These are three coins each."
14354: A disguise parlor has launched an "influencer face" package. In recent duels, both sides took off their masks to find they looked exactly alike, and the fight had to be canceled because no one could tell who was who.
14355: A great hero who trained Iron Cloth Shirt for thirty years slipped on a banana peel in the street. His skin didn't break, but his bones ached so much from the jolt that he cried in the street for a whole double-hour.
14356: A famous one-armed hero's divine condor has gone on strike, demanding better meals. The condor's protest letter: I fly people around every day until my wings swell, and all I get is cold dry rations?
14357: An old senior left a will saying "the treasure is under the old tree in the back mountains". The younger generation dug for three days and nights and found only a note: "Exercise and build your health. Digging holes is training too."
14358: Jianghu reminder: if you walk into an inn and the landlady is too beautiful, the waiter is too eager and the cook holds the knife like a sword, drop your bowl, jump out the window and don't look back.
14359: The current Martial Alliance Leader was spotted eating wontons at a roadside stall and arguing with the owner for ages over two coins of change. The Leader says: even number one in the martial world has to live, and nobody's money blows in on the wind.
14360: Behold, everyone! The Sect Master's honored title is printed boldly on the card for place {%s}. Every brick and tile of your sect now carries sword intent, every blade of grass shows backbone. The jianghu hasn't seen a ruler who shakes its very foundations in a long time. Sect Master, from now on every word you say will likely be compiled into the Martial World Chronicle for later generations to study by incense light.
14361: The Sect Master stands at place {%s}. That's not progress, that's a change of dynasty! Now when your disciples come down the mountain, even long-famous old swordsmen step aside and say "I've long admired you." The view from the peak is fine, but it's cold up high; please sit calmly above it all, Sect Master, and look down on the game board of all beings.
14362: Everyone who reaches place {%s} is a dragon or phoenix among people, and the Sect Master is the hardest of them all to read. The shabby little sect of the past is now a holy land that ten thousand sects pay homage to. Our editors dare to ask: which famous mountain will the Sect Master annex next? We'd like to buy some land there in advance.
14363: Watching your sect hold place {%s}, this reporter is out of words. With your sect's depth these days, even the sweepers probably have earth-shaking talent. Sect Master, the sky over the martial world changes at your whim. Ruthless war or ruling by doing nothing? Every eye in the jianghu is waiting for your next move.
14364: Place {%s}: a back that many people never even glimpse in a lifetime of trying. Sect Master, your sect is now a living legend. The powers that once looked on coldly are now queuing up with gifts to make peace. That's the jianghu: the winner holds not only the sword but the right to define justice.
14365: Sect Master, is the seat at place {%s} comfortable? In all the years this Jianghu Gazette has run, we've never seen a rise as unstoppable as your sect's. Now even a casual wave of your sleeve can raise towering waves in the jianghu. Congratulations: you are, without question, the one who makes the rules.
14366: All things have spirit, and they know the strong. With the Sect Master at place {%s}, it's not just people who fear you; even the mountains, rivers, grass and trees revere you. The days of sheltering from the rain in that shabby little hut feel like another lifetime. Now which hero in the land would dare stand before your sect with a drawn blade?
14367: Quite right! The Sect Master ranks at place {%s}, which has already left most so-called "heroes" in despair. You don't need a heroes' invitation, because wherever you stand is the heroes' gathering. From now on the jianghu won't care about seniority, only about the divine weapon in your hand.
14368: Sect Master, you've even stirred up the old monsters! The worth of place {%s} is built on the bones of the defeated you've trampled underfoot. Your sect no longer has to prove anything to anyone. When you sit down, you're the backbone of the whole martial world.
14369: Watching the ranking climb to place {%s}, has the Sect Master started planning a bigger back garden? Don't say I didn't warn you: take too big a stride and you might... ahem. Anyway, until you become an immortal, remember to build the sect walls higher first. The higher the ranking, the more freeloaders come for a free meal.
14370: Sect Master, congratulations on winning this year's "Most Likely to Get Fleeced" award... no wait, the "Most Promising" award. Place {%s} means you've climbed out of poverty into modest comfort. As long as you don't drop the ball at the crucial moment, next issue's headline might be your close-up (though maybe for illegal construction).
14371: Look at that swollen ego! Sect Master, place {%s} is something to be proud of, but please tell your disciples: when you meet senior brothers from the top ten, step aside. Our current strategy is "farm quietly, don't get cocky". Got it?
14372: We may have sharp tongues, but seeing the Sect Master lead the charge to place {%s} actually touches us a little. It shows that in this scheming jianghu, if you work hard enough (or just hang on long enough), even a ruined temple can become a sect. Keep charging, Sect Master. We'll be waiting at the place-50 line with our sharpest insults ready!
14373: Sect Master, congratulations on your sect reaching place {%s}! We hear wandering martial artists have started poking their heads in at your gate lately? They may only want to borrow the toilet, but it means your sect's name is no longer "location not found". Please keep up the sect's image; even if your disciples are cultivating immortality, have them wash their faces first.
14374: Seeing your sect at place {%s} brings our editors great comfort. Sect Master, we hear your disciples' morale is much higher lately? We suggest striking while the iron is hot with a sect team-building event, like catching pigs in the back mountains. Remember, the higher the ranking, the more the disciples' hearts run wild like a donkey off its leash. Keep a tight grip on the reins.
14375: With the ranking up to place {%s}, the Sect Master needs to start fighting counterfeits. Rumor has it someone down the mountain is posing as your disciple to swindle people. All they got was a bundle of scallions, but it does prove your sect's "brand value". When someone poses as you to marry for money, then you'll truly be famous across the jianghu.
14376: Sect Master, look, everyone's searching for the "dark horse". Place {%s} is only your starting line. Our editors already have next issue's front-page picture ready for you. Move up another ten places or so, and even if you're picking your nose in the photo, we'll write that you're "sensing the qi of heaven and earth".
14377: Sect Master, your sect currently ranks at place {%s}. According to the Roadside News Agency, your sect's canteen has started smelling of meat lately? That's a dangerous sign! Where there's meat there's a jianghu, and where there's a jianghu there's strife. Please protect your pots and pans; they're important fixed assets of the sect, after all.
14378: Congratulations, Sect Master, your sect has made it to place {%s}. It's not that high, but it's enough for your enemies to write you in their little grudge books. When out and about, remind your disciples to drink less from strangers and watch the road more. After all, nobody who holds their ground at place {%s} is easy to deal with.
14379: Sect Master, see how bold that youngster is? Well, now you have to be bolder. Place {%s} is like a youth just come down the mountain: no peerless divine art yet, but plenty of a newborn calf's fire. Don't let that fire go out. Keep it burning, and prosperity lies ahead.
14380: Sect Master, your sect's place {%s} sounds like zither music from an ancient tomb: it has a fresh feel. But the jianghu is dangerous, and refinement alone isn't enough. Before your fame spreads across the land, swap your disciples' fire pokers for real iron, or when a true master comes calling to "hear the zither", all we'll be able to do is put on an acrobatics show.
14381: Oh dear, Sect Master, your sect at place {%s} is in an awkward spot that attracts thieves: famous enough that every passerby knows you, but without the depth to have built walls of iron yet. We suggest you stop letting disciples stay at random inns for now. If the whole sect comes back one day with no eyebrows, where would the dignity of place {%s} be?
14382: Sect Master, we hear your disciples have started "mind training" instead of eating meat to save money? Looking at the place {%s} report card, we suggest you hold off on unifying the martial world and work out how to patch the sect's leaky roof first. Catching a cold costs money for medicine too.
14383: Your sect is extremely competitive in the recruitment market: as long as people can't read and don't look at rankings, you can talk almost anyone into joining. Place {%s} hasn't hit the mainstream yet, but your sect's food (cold water and steamed buns) is famous far and wide. Sect Master, how about a career change to a restaurant chain?
14384: Wrong, we mean you, Sect Master! While everyone else is clawing their way up, your sect sits firmly on the cold bench at place {%s}. Even Shaolin's eminent monks would envy that composure. If this detached "I'll just quietly watch you all compete" mindset could turn into even a tiny bit of fighting power, you wouldn't be ranked here.
14385: It's good to have ideals, but you have to look at the rankings too. At place {%s}, your sect's biggest strength is "infinite room for improvement". Moving up even one place would be a historic breakthrough! Until then, Sect Master, please keep up the fine tradition of "I may be weak, but I can brag".
14386: Oh! Did the Sect Master find a secret manual lately? Your sect has quietly crept up to place {%s}. To the Martial Alliance Leader you're still a grain of sand, but to old Uncle Wang at the village entrance, you're the toughest building foreman for ten li around. Keep up the momentum and don't keep everyone waiting too long!
14387: Sect Master, congratulations on rising to place {%s}! Our reporter observes that your disciples' weapons have finally upgraded from "splintery wooden sticks" to "not-very-sharp iron swords". That's a leap in quality! You're still a few centuries away from cutting iron like mud, but it's more than enough to scare off bandits.
14388: Looks like your sect at place {%s} is full of energy lately! Sect Master, progress is good, but don't show off too much. The ones ranked ahead of you are staring at the back of your head right now. Keep charging or quit while you're ahead? That depends on your grind... no, your vision.
14389: Sect Master, your recent showing has cost a lot of gamblers their shirts. Place {%s} is a delicate spot, like a child who's just learned to walk: everyone wants to see whether you'll break into a run or fall flat on your face in public. Go for it, every degenerate gambler in the jianghu is watching you!
14390: [Cash for Goods] A famous swordsman went into qi deviation while training and is selling a nearly new "Dragon-Slaying Saber" cheap (note: it's actually a kitchen knife painted black). Interested parties, please meet at the Yuelai Inn.
14391: [Anti-Scam Alert] A monk calling himself the "Sweeping Monk" has come down the mountain recruiting students. He's actually a farmhand who went missing from Granny Wang's next door. All sects, keep your eyes open and don't pay any illegal "incense fees".
14392: The owner of a pawnshop in the capital says they've recently taken in a large number of wooden plaques reading "Supreme of the Martial World", apparently from the bankruptcy liquidation of some up-and-coming sect.
14393: The Conservation Society appeals: swordsmen, please don't duel in bamboo groves. The giant panda next door says its home has been demolished.
14394: The jianghu's first iron law: never mess with an old monk walking alone in the wilderness, a girl drinking alone, or a toddling child. According to past Gazette statistics, 90% of them are hidden masters and the other 10% are Demonic Cult fiends running a sting.
14395: When eating at an inn, a ground-floor window seat is best, so you can jump out the window at any moment. Remember, never pick the end of the second-floor corridor. That's prime real estate for jianghu killings; the swordsmen who've died there each year could circle the capital three times.
14396: Real masters don't shout their move names in a duel. If your opponent is yelling "Behold my Earth-Shaking Mountain-Splitting Slash", they're most likely bluffing, or covering up that they just want to throw lime in your eyes.
14397: Statistics show the average jianghu lifespan is only 28. The rest survived by "playing dead", "hiding in the deep mountains" or "becoming an NPC". So knowing when to bend isn't cowardice, it's longevity.
14398: Don't believe the picture books with "a hundred ultimates in a row". Internal energy is limited; after a full Ten Thousand Swords Return, even a master wants to crouch somewhere and catch their breath. That's when you go in for one more punch, and your odds are great.
14399: "Our reporter went to enormous lengths and finally found this... er, barely weatherproof sect in a dead corner of the map. Congratulations, Sect Master, your standing in the jianghu is very secure. So secure that passing bandits can't be bothered to come in and rob you. Your sect's name may not yet ring as loud as Auntie Wang's tofu shop at the village entrance, but look at it another way: looking back from 91st, your room for improvement is practically a bottomless pit! We suggest the Sect Master first straighten that peeling sect plaque before thinking about unifying the jianghu. Go for it, future Martial Alliance Leader (provisional)!"
14400: Seeing your sect's current result of place {%s}, we're deeply pleased. Through the zen management of "no training, no work, no recruiting", the Sect Master has made an outstanding contribution to energy saving in the jianghu. That "as long as I don't try, nobody can overtake me" aura is truly charming. We suggest you keep up this deep-sleep management style.
14401: It seems the Sect Master has taken inspiration from the elders and is firmly rooted in the vast expanse of place {%s}. We'd call this unhurried composure "the jianghu's invisible man". Keep it up: at your current rate of progress, in another five hundred years the martial histories might give your sect a footnote.
14402: To report on your sect's current state, our reporter visited in person and got lost three times. We have to say, the ranking of place {%s} is as mysterious as your sect's location. Being here isn't bad, really. You're not standing very high, so when you fall, it's only about as far as rolling off a step onto flat ground.

14924: Click a disciple's portrait or select one in the scene, and the disciple info panel pops up on the left with their details

14927: Health: the most basic measure of a disciple's condition. If it gets too low, the character dies
14928: Happiness: an overall picture of a disciple's mental state. Very low Happiness can trigger a breakdown, during which the character is depressed, out of control and less able to work

14944: To hold prisoners you must have a prison; it's the foundation of the prisoner system. Once a room is built, switch its type to Prison and build a suitable prison as required.
14946: To take a prisoner, you first knock the target down. Disciples from other sects who invade and are knocked down but not killed can be imprisoned if you've built a prison.
14948: Loyalty: the prisoner's core stat. Torture lowers it. Once loyalty falls to a certain threshold, the game tells you "this prisoner can now be recruited".
14949: Meals: prisoners need to eat. You can set what food they may eat on the "Control" page. Disciples have to carry the food into the prison.
14950: Treatment: prisoners may be injured, and you can choose whether to use healing medicine on them.
14951: Torture: the direct way to lower loyalty fast. Each session lowers the prisoner's loyalty. You choose a disciple to do it, and their Diplomacy skill affects the result. There's a cooldown after each session.
14952: Execution: if a prisoner just won't come over, or their sect is hostile, you can execute them. This needs an "Execution Platform" and a disciple to carry it out. Execution raises your sect's reputation but sharply lowers relations with the prisoner's original sect.
14953: Release: you can also choose to release a prisoner. This restores some relations with their sect.
14955: Timing: when a prisoner's loyalty falls to the recruitment threshold, you'll get a notification.
14956: Choosing who recruits: you have to pick a disciple to carry out the recruitment by hand. You'll see that disciple's chance of success.
14957: Success chance: it isn't fixed. It's worked out from the base chance, the loyalty bonus, the disciple's Diplomacy, the prisoner's sect level, your own sect level and more.

14959: Failure: after a failed recruitment, the prisoner's loyalty recovers some, and you have to wait a while before trying again.

14974: Star Energy buildings are a special class of buildings that run on Star Energy. Unlike ordinary buildings, they produce faster and use fewer resources, making them the backbone of an advanced sect. Unlock them through the [Star Energy techs] in the tech tree
14975: Star Energy buildings need a Star Energy supply to work. You need dedicated production, transmission and storage facilities to form a complete system, and must meet certain placement and energy balance rules, or they won't work.
14976: How Star Energy buildings work: dedicated Star Energy source buildings produce it, and transmission facilities carry it to every Star Energy building. All Star Energy buildings must be within transmission range and properly connected, and total supply must be no lower than total use, for them to keep running.
14978: The Star Energy system rests on five core energy buildings that produce, transmit and store Star Energy. Every one is needed for Star Energy buildings to run. Each has a clear role, and together they form a complete supply system.
14979: Star-Gathering Tube: produces Star Energy around the clock at a gentle pace, collecting it 24 hours a day with a steady output unaffected by day and night. It makes up for the Moonlight Platform working only at night; together they give a steady supply all day.
14980: Moonlight Platform: produces Star Energy only at night (a set time in-game), efficiently turning moonlight into Star Energy with a higher output than an ordinary collector. It's the core of the night-time supply and lies dormant by day, producing nothing.
14981: Star Energy Storage Pool: a building dedicated to storing Star Energy. It stores surplus energy from the source buildings so none goes to waste, and releases it when production falls short, keeping supply and demand balanced so Star Energy buildings never stop.
14982: Mohist Thousand-Star Cauldron: an advanced Star Energy producer that runs on "Star Crystal ore" as fuel. Once lit, it produces a lot of Star Energy quickly, an important top-up when demand spikes (such as many Star Energy buildings running at once). It stops producing when the fuel runs out.
14984: Star Energy transmission relies on the Star Energy Tower (the core transmission building). Every Star Energy building, including the Moonlight Platform, Star-Gathering Tube and Mohist Thousand-Star Cauldron among the source buildings as well as all other functional Star Energy buildings, must be built within a tower's range and properly connected to it to receive power.
14985: Placement: lay out Star Energy Towers so their range reaches every Star Energy building you need running. A Star Energy building outside the range can't start, even if supply is plentiful.
14986: Connection rules: towers and Star Energy buildings need an unblocked, continuous connection. You can chain several towers to extend the range over a large area and power Star Energy buildings in many places.
14988: Every Star Energy building has a fixed Star Energy use, and amounts differ by building. For the system to run, total supply must be at least total use; otherwise a protective mechanism kicks in.
14989: When it's out of balance: if all Star Energy buildings together need more than is produced (including what the storage pool releases), every Star Energy building "goes on strike" and stops working entirely until supply and demand balance again.
14990: How to recover: there are two ways. One, raise production (add collectors or Star-Gathering Tubes, light the Mohist Thousand-Star Cauldron, or release stored energy from the storage pool). Two, cut use (such as temporarily switching off some non-essential high-use buildings). Once total supply is no lower than total use, all Star Energy buildings resume automatically.
14992: Planning: before building Star Energy buildings, plan where the Star Energy Towers go first, so they cover every Star Energy building you plan, and buildings don't end up unusable later for lack of coverage.
14993: Supply control: check Star Energy supply and demand regularly, match source buildings to what your Star Energy buildings use, and keep a reserve (in the storage pool) so an imbalance doesn't send buildings on strike.
14994: Fuel reserves: if you use the Mohist Thousand-Star Cauldron, stock enough Star Crystal ore in advance so the supply isn't cut when the fuel runs out, and time the cauldron well, using it first at peak demand.
14995: Expansion: as you add Star Energy buildings, add towers to extend coverage in time, and add production and storage too, so supply keeps up with use and the system stays stable.

15045: In the south, Wudang is honored; in the north, Damo is revered. Founded by the grandmaster Zhang Sanfeng at over a hundred years old, it teaches "the Dao follows nature; softness overcomes hardness". The sect sits on Mount Wudang among drifting immortal clouds. Its disciples cultivate body and mind, and their internal energy runs deep and long like a great river that never stops. The later the fight, the more its unbeatable, flowing art of striking after the enemy shows.
15047: The western peak is rugged, its sword qi soaring to the sky. As head of the Five Mountain Sword Sects, Huashan's sword art is famous for being "surprising and perilous". But the sect has long been torn by the feud between the Qi faction and the Sword faction, and the infighting runs deep.
15049: All martial arts under heaven come from Damo; this ancient Chan monastery leads them all. On Mount Song, its Sutra Library holds half the martial world's secret arts. The monks meditate and farm by day, and when enemies come they form the Eighteen Arhat Bronze Men Array, indestructible and impervious to all evil. As the leading light of the martial world, its depth is unfathomable, and it's home to the legendary old sweeping monk, the pinnacle of martial arts today.
15051: A fallen royal clan holding out in the Jiangnan water country, owners of the Huanshi Water Pavilion, which gathers fragments of every sect's martial arts. The Murong are skilled in letters and arms, elegant in bearing and sworn to restore their kingdom. Their family art turns heaven and earth, using an opponent's force against them so they die by their own signature move. They seem content in their corner, but they're scheming for the whole realm, and every move hides a staggering ambition.
15053: A secretive clan deep in the mountains of Ba-Shu, peerless in the martial world for poison and hidden weapons. Silver needles steeped in deadly poison, darts hiding death, and its signature hidden weapon, the Peacock Plume, is a killing move. Its members value bloodline and keep secrets, rarely setting foot in the Central Plains, yet no one dares provoke them. Anyone who crosses the Tang Sect can flee to the ends of the earth and still not escape the soul-chasing dart.
15054: The most secretive and vast society in the jianghu, with branches in towns across the land. Its members include peddlers and porters as well as heroes and men of honor, all calling one another brother, with code words and secret signs like no other. It has no peerless internal art to hand down, but it has eyes and ears everywhere and the people's hearts. Running this sect doesn't mean sitting in the deep mountains; it means gathering a hero's spirit in this dusty mortal world.
15056: Kongtong of Longyou, a line of the immortal mountains, famous across the jianghu for the Seven Injuries Fist: each punch deals seven parts harm to the enemy and three to yourself, utterly domineering. Its disciples mostly travel the northwestern frontier protecting the people there. Its martial arts prize hardness and boldness, but because of the danger of backlash, every generation warns its members to "kill with care". Not one of the Central Plains' top sects, but a firm banner of the northwestern martial world.
15057: Qingcheng in Shu, with its spirited mountains and lovely waters. The sect's sword art is nimble and graceful, as changeable as the mists of Qingcheng. Its disciples mostly wear blue robes, keep a low profile and excel at turning an opponent's force against them, beating strong foes with clever force. The sect has long kept to itself in Shu and rarely meddles in the Central Plains' conflicts. Only when its homeland is in trouble do Qingcheng masters ride out on their swords, and where their blades point follows no fixed rule, only right and wrong.
15058: The orthodox martial school of the northern frontier, founded on the Five Tigers Saber, a fierce, domineering saber art where every move goes for the vitals. Most of its disciples come from the army or escort agencies. They prize loyalty and righteousness, have never failed an escort however dangerous, and carry great weight among the greenwood outlaws. But in their rules, "loyalty and righteousness" apply only to fellow members and those who hire them; the life or death of anyone else has never been their concern.
15059: An unorthodox sect hidden in the deserts of the Western Regions, peerless for hidden weapons and lightness skill. Its members move like ghosts and their poisoned hidden weapons never miss. Its signature art, Meteor Chases the Moon, can take a head in an instant. Its members are hard to track and act only on "commissions". Loyal official or traitor, if the fee is paid, there's no head they can't take.
15060: On Emei's Golden Summit, Buddhism and Daoism share one source. It's one of the few great sects in the martial world made up mostly of women. Its martial arts balance hard and soft, with both the sharp, tricky Emei thrust and a compassionate method like the Buddha's light. Its disciples care for all people and often go down the mountain to help those in need. Though mostly women, they're every bit the equal of men and respected by both the righteous and the unorthodox.
15061: The largest merchant guild in the jianghu, headquartered in Yangzhou in Jiangnan, with branches at every river and land port in the realm. It cares little for martial arts and much for gold, silver, goods and connections, with friends from high court officials down to greenwood bandits. The Jubao Gang is rich enough to rival a kingdom: it can supply anyone with money, grain and goods, and cut off anyone's livelihood. It acts on profit alone, never on sides.
15063: A prominent Jiangdong family with a century of heritage, known for spear arts and lightness skill. Its sons and daughters are skilled in letters and arms and full of grace. The clan holds the Jiangdong water country and is close to the local officials, a jianghu name with court connections. Its members always put family honor first. Peace in Jiangdong is both their bottom line and their ambition.
15065: A martial clan that rose in the northern desert, proud of its palm arts and horsemanship. Its members are mostly brave fighters with bold natures. The clan has guarded the northern desert for generations, and its martial style carries the wildness of the steppe, with palm force strong enough to split steles. The Dongfang value blood and honor above all and would rather break than bend. They won't give an inch to foreign invaders, but they have their own calculations about the conflicts of the Central Plains.
15067: A Daoist retreat at the foot of Mount Zhongnan, whose disciples refine qi and train the mind and excel at talismans and swordplay. Their martial arts are about "guiding the sword with qi and guarding the body with talismans". They're skilled at laying arrays to fight enemies, and their Tiangang Big Dipper Array can trap and kill top masters. The temple doesn't concern itself with jianghu feuds, only with training the heavenly Dao, but when it meets those who defy law and the Dao, Qingxu's talismans and swords show no mercy.
15069: The greatest intelligence organization in the land, hidden in a deep mountain valley. Its members know the heavens above and the earth below, and are masters of every divination and formation art. They take no part in jianghu killings and only sell information: from finding a person or object to state military secrets, anything can be known for the right price. The pavilion is mysterious, and no one knows its master's true face, only that its intelligence can make a sect rise or a clan fall.
15071: A gang holding the East Sea, headquartered on a lone island, every member a superb swimmer. They roam the East Sea, and their martial arts carry the force of the waves, moves rising and falling like the tide without end. They live off the sea, robbing passing merchant ships but also protecting coastal fishermen. Everything depends on a word from the gang leader; on the East Sea, they are the rules.
15073: An alliance of jianghu wanderers, each with special skills, who do as they please and keep clear accounts of favors and grudges. They can't stand red tape and only accept "the hardest fist rules". With no fixed sect gate, they make their home wherever they are. For someone they like, they'll take a knife for them without a second thought; for someone they don't, even a member of a renowned righteous sect, they'll kill all the same.
15075: An unorthodox sect that blends wine into martial arts. Its members won't train without wine, and the drunker they get, the better they fight. Their arts follow "in drunkenness the world is vast, in the gourd the days are long"; their drunken fist and drunken sword are superb, moves that look chaotic but hide killing intent. The disciples love wine more than life and are free and unrestrained. Doing heroic deeds while drunk is common, and so is hurting someone by accident; it all comes down to the wine and their own hearts.
15076: A sect that grew out of a smithing clan of the Western Regions, famous for forging divine weapons and training Iron Body arts. Most of its members were blacksmiths, with thick arms and enormous strength; they can forge swords that cut iron like mud and also stand up to divine weapons with their hard qigong. The Xuantie Sect is devoted to the art of forging and will make a divine weapon for anyone who pays. What the weapon is used for, they've never cared.
15078: A band of outlaws who rule their mountain and live by highway robbery. Their moves are messy but vicious, and all they want is enough to eat.
15080: A small sect of a few martial instructors who make a living teaching locals to fight. No secret arts, they only want a quiet life.
15082: A jianghu trade devoted to one craft, whether smithing or making poisons and treating wounds. They stay out of conflicts and earn honest money.
15084: A small band of down-and-out martial artists who scrape by in the jianghu taking guard and errand jobs on what little reputation they have.
15086: A knock-off sect flying a renowned sect's banner. They've picked up a few surface moves and make a living conning outsiders.
15088: The sect is rooted on the icy peaks of Tianshan, its disciples training the sword among frost and snow with a cool, otherworldly grace. It has no love for the mortal world, guarding its cold ridges alone, and is famed across the Western Regions for its Cold Ice Sword Art.
15090: A few martial artists who were once hunters, living by hunting and guarding their village. Their fists carry the toughness of the wild mountains.
15092: A small sect led by a down-and-out scholar. No real skills, they get by on crooked tricks.
15094: A troupe of traveling performers who've learned a few flashy moves and barely get by on street shows and bodyguard work.
15096: Remnants guarding a ruined temple. Their martial arts are mediocre, and they live by begging and scavenging.
15097: A small sect that lives by gathering herbs and treating bruises and sprains. Their fists are only enough for self-defense, and they never dare get involved in jianghu conflicts.
15099: A group of disciples expelled from their sects. Their moves are a mixed bag, each with strengths and weaknesses, and they take the dirty jobs renowned sects won't touch.
15106: A small sect hidden in the countryside, guarding an incomplete ancestral martial art. It ignores the world and only hopes to keep the line alive.
15161: A faction from Fengsha, entrenched among desert mountain passes, with beacon fires for signals and wind and sand for company. Its members are brave fighters who come and go like the wind.
15163: The Shenlong Cult holds Shenlong Island overseas and controls its followers with venomous snakes, Gu sorcery and mind-numbing drugs. Its leader calls himself the "Heaven-Reaching Divine Dragon", with Dragon Envoys under him running punishment, wealth and spying. Ranks in the cult are strict, and its hidden agents are planted in every sect. Joining means swearing an oath over dragon-blood wine, and traitors are eaten alive by ten thousand snakes. The jianghu blanches at its name. The righteous path has tried to wipe it out many times, but the island's fog and miasma and the cult's insiders have mostly defeated them.
15165: Desperadoes gathered in the mountain forests who rob passing caravans at dangerous passes on the highway, coming and going without a trace.
15167: Set among the folds of the mountains, cut off from the world with only one hidden path to the outside. The valley is full of strange rocks and the miasma never clears.
15207: Battlefield for sect wars against Wudang
15208: Desert Gobi, sand filling the sky
15215: An ancient temple hanging in the air, once full of worshippers, now crumbling and desolate.
15217: Half of an ancient temple half-hidden in the snow, a pagoda jutting at an angle, a stone Buddha's face half showing. All is silent but for the falling snow. Time is frozen in the icicles; secrets are buried beneath the snow.
15219: The summit of Wudang's Mount Zhenwu. Elite disciples stand in formation at the front and Daoist masters hold the rear. Probably no one under heaven can reach the main hall.
15221: A city in the snowy mountains
15235: A desert highway used by merchants and travelers, often haunted by bandits
15236: A month ago, enemies in black raided the sect by night, and amid flashing blades a century's legacy went up in flames. Your father, the Sect Master, fought to the last to cover your escape and finally fell in a pool of blood. Holding back your grief, you led a few elite disciples away from the pursuit and, after much wandering, reached this hidden valley cut off from the world.
15237: The wind moans through the valley. Your disciples' faces are full of exhaustion and confusion, yet they still look to you with hope. You are the sect's last hope, and the heavy task of rebuilding it now rests on your shoulders.

Once one disciple's routine is set, you can copy it to the others. Open the Schedule menu at the bottom of the screen and fill each hour slot with Work, Sleep, Recreation or Training.

15328: The jianghu is extremely dangerous, and you'll need good weapons to protect yourselves; enemies may attack in force one day. Make some weapons and practice by hunting some small animals first. At this point his sword is fierce and his edge on full display; all he sees is the will to win, fixated on intricate moves, speed of the draw and force of the cut. You approach respectfully to ask for guidance, but Miyamoto won't cross swords with a nobody and offers only a one-on-one wager: if you can take his sword strokes, he'll acknowledge you as a true swordsman. In this fight he no longer cares for a fast, vicious, fierce draw; he means to test whether you stay calm, unhurried and unshaken in battle. Beating him takes not intricate moves but a steady heart.

Miyamoto will hold nothing back; only by guiding the sword with your heart, unswayed by moves and untied to victory or defeat, can you go beyond swordsmanship itself and touch the truth of the sword. 16610: Learn to make simple wooden furniture. Learn to fix timber with wooden wedges and rattan rope and unlock basic wooden furniture. It creaks when you sit on it, but at least you don't have to sleep on the floor.
16611: Unlocks the war drum training spot. Drumbeats shake the meridians and set qi and blood boiling! Besides food and clothes, disciples need a skill to rely on; train some martial arts so nobody pushes you around.
16612: Lets you plant cotton and tea bushes. Soft, fluffy cotton can be spun and woven to keep out the cold. Plant it and you not only get clothes, it also shelters the wheat from the wind, and the wheat grows even better!
16613: Learn to make wooden weapons. Sharpen a branch and it's a spear; bend a plank and it's a bow! They break easily, but that beats feeding the beasts bare-handed.
16614: Learn stone weapons and tools. Pick the hardest stone and smash a softer one! Unlocks basic stone weapons. They chip easily, but at least your hands won't go numb when you hit something!
16615: Learn to make good everyday wooden furniture. A few pieces of wood make a rack, so no more tossing things all over the floor. You can put a few favorite things on the shelves, but handle them gently; those shelves might fall over any day.
16616: Learn wooden building structures. Farewell to life in a stone cave! The wooden floor creaks, the wooden windows leak air and the wooden door hangs crooked, but at least it looks like a "house"!
16617: Learn alchemy. Training needs elixirs too, so the disciples start learning to simmer medicine over a low flame. The results sometimes come out black as charcoal, but never mind the taste, they can at least be called "elixirs".
16618: Learn ranged attacks. Train archery on targets and hidden weapons on straw men. To fool the Sect Master, disciples can shoot the arrow first and draw the target around it afterward. If there are no handy hidden weapons, a kitchen knife will do.
16619: Learn to make medicine. Those who like medicine have studied pharmacy: a combined course of anti-bleeding, mind-calming and anti-radiation drugs. Who knows if there are side effects.
16620: Learn to make colorful cotton cloth. It only looks nice; it's not actually useful. When the workmanship is poor, the color runs in the rain too.
16621: Learn to make flour and food. Unlocks one of humanity's greatest inventions on the side: rations you can use as a shield! Everyone eats more.
16622: Learn to make bows and traps. Practice archery hard and never miss! With great archery comes great trapping; when a beast comes, it falls right in the pit. Of course, if one of our own steps in, that counts as an extra meal too...
16623: Learn to make fine wooden furniture. Carved headboards and jade-inlaid mortise joints let the disciples sleep a little more comfortably. Study can't stop either; the handwriting isn't pretty, but at least it's legible.
16624: Unlocks carrier pigeon training: messages across a thousand li in an instant! The pigeons often get lost at first, but that still beats having disciples run their legs off.
16625: Unlocks the sect leaderboard. A gilded ranking board stands before the sect gate, updating disciples' rankings in real time. Their enthusiasm and efficiency in training shoot up, and the competition between them seems even fiercer...
16626: Learn basic martial moves. Grasp some basic sword moves. The motion looks like chopping firewood, but at least they can split a wooden post now. Though the sword often gets stuck in the wood.
16627: Improve medical skill. Golden needles through the acupoints, silver threads to hang on to life. The disciples start studying acupuncture and often draw blood by accident. Whether the needle hits the spot is down to fate anyway.
16628: Learn to make clothes from hides. With hide tanning, the disciples start dressing respectably. Except they sometimes fight over who gets to wear the tiger skin and who gets the wolf skin.
16629: Learn shoemaking and hatmaking. Nobody wants to wear their new shoes, and when they step in a mud puddle in the rain, their hearts hurt more than their feet.
16630: Unlocks basic animal taming. No more fighting wild boars for territory! Though the first wolf tamed always thinks it's a dog...
16631: Can make home-style dishes. Farewell to the dark age of "anything can be burned"! The knife work looks like a dog chewed it, but at least it's edible. Probably...
16632: Learn hunting skills and metal ranged weapons. The disciples specialize in ranged killing! A rain of arrows plus ground nets and traps makes a deadly combo! Needs three days' rest after use, because picking up the arrows hurts their backs.
16633: Unlocks Star Crystal mining: chisel out Star Crystals with black iron picks. The mining notes, paid for with generations of miners' lives, detail how Star Crystal veins run and where they crack.
16634: Learn to make large wooden furniture. Bookshelves and supply chests form a storage matrix that doubles the sect's efficiency! Disciples can read better experience books, though some only read the "dual cultivation" chapter over and over.
16635: Unlocks the administration spirit map, marking disciples' movements with star patterns so you can direct people remotely. Learn to project star markers with the sundial, and every disciple within a hundred li can see the guiding pillar of light.
16636: Unlocks Star Energy lighting: lamps made from meteorite powder light up on their own! But they overload at full moon and turn street lamps into "flashbangs".
16637: Master hidden weapons further; even pebbles by the road will do! Hidden weapons often get stuck in your sleeve, though, and when collecting them you keep finding the next sect's trouser belts.
16638: Learn to make bandages and stimulants. The disciples can heal faster and get back to work empowering the sect. Now and then they can have a couple of shots for a boost, all for the sake of reviving the sect.
16639: Unlocks the Star Energy windmill: meteorite energy drives the millstone! No more people or donkeys needed to grind flour, and it runs 24 hours non-stop.
16640: Unlocks all-in-one animal facilities. Oxen plow the fields, dogs guard the gate and pigeons deliver the post. The animals have their own jobs and missions, but first they need comfortable homes.
16641: Unlocks coin minting. Farewell to primitive barter! Except some light-fingered disciples swipe scraps to make rings for their partners.
16642: A special furnace fueled by Star Energy stones that can smelt Star Crystal veins. Its fire never goes out, hot enough to melt gold and iron; ordinary metal melts at a touch.
16643: A complete overhaul of Star Energy craft: reshape meteoric iron with the "Fine Forging Method" to make precise Star Energy parts. Accurate to a hair, though the craftsmen have to work blindfolded because the starlight is so dazzling.
16644: Unlocks efficient Star Energy storage, raising mechanism core endurance by 300%. But when overloaded, puppets break into an uncontrollable Star Energy ritual dance, with outrageously perfect form.
16645: Unlocks basic mechanism puppetry: simple wooden mechanical men with camphor-wood bones and beast-sinew tendons. They move as slowly as old men but can carry a thousand jin and never sleep.
16646: Unlocks the Reading Desk and Transcription Desk. The reading loop is complete and knowledge spreads twice as fast! But some lazybones always copy the Sword Manual into a cookbook and insist "if you're a dish, just practice more".
16647: Grasp Wudang's martial arts. Disciples can deepen their Wudang training progress; their sword intent resonates as they train, they sometimes glimpse a phantom of Zhang Sanfeng, and their attainment climbs another step.
16648: Grasp Shaolin's martial arts. The disciples secretly picked up some renowned righteous sect arts and even worked out a recipe: Golden Bell Shield plus Lesser Return Pill, so the worse you're hurt, the faster you recover!
16649: Learn to make finer silk clothing. The Starlight Engraving Table adds Star Energy patterns automatically while embroidering. From "cloth to cover the body" to "rainbow robes with affixes", even needle and thread can weave the laws of heaven!
16650: Can freeze food and restores Relaxation. The Star Energy storage station is online: vegetables don't wilt for a year and fresh meat never rots! The disciples hoard everything, until they find a salted fish frozen for ten years has come back to life...
16651: Can raise the Taming skill. The viewing garden earns ticket money, the hunting ground trains fierce beasts, and ticket income doubles when the pandas roll around.
16652: Learn to make Star Energy ranged weapons and traps. Arrows are tipped with meteoric iron shards, and Star Energy traps can create energy vortexes. The only downside: the blue flash when firing is so bright it easily gives away your ambush.
16653: Unlocks the equipment modification system. Gear is tougher and more hard-wearing, and wearing it makes you feel much livelier. Every now and then, though, it produces failures like a "self-igniting sword" or "freezing armor".
16654: Unlocks Star Energy forging: smelt star-vein ore in meteor flame, and ordinary iron tempered this way becomes a divine weapon. "Spirit star in the left hand, evil iron in the right. One thought toward good, one thought toward demonhood."
16655: Unlocks bluestone brick firing: clay mixed with lime and tempered in the kiln. Hard and weatherproof, the foundation of any building.
16656: Unlocks the Six-Gate Contemplation Pavilion, whose six jade gates match the body's six great meridians! Disciples meditating there can activate basic internal arts, but people often count the gates wrong, send their qi and blood backwards and hiccup like mad.
16657: Learn to make Taiji gear. Swords cast from singing iron and robes woven from black silkworm silk: the forging of Wudang's ultimate artifacts. Come within three chi and you can hear the sword hum.
16658: Grasp the essence of Chan martial arts. Every punch carries Buddhist mantras, and demons who see it just shut themselves away. But the eminent monks say: "This aesthetic of violence goes against the Buddha's compassion."
16659: Learn to make organ prosthetics. Hollow peach-wood heart, lungs, liver and kidneys keep basic body functions going! They last 12 double-hours, then pop open with a "click" to remind you to wind them up.
16660: Bring in running water to build a fishery: carp in spring, perch in summer, fresh fish all year! Just pick up a fish basket and you'll hear the disciples shout: never coming home empty-handed!
16661: Unlocks the Star Energy Stove and fine dishes. Every disciple is a god of cooking, stewing the qi of heaven and earth in one pot! Everyone for miles around wants a free meal; the dishes are top-notch.
16662: Unlocks Star Energy weapons of destruction. Meteoric iron shells, one blast flattens ten li! As powerful as a meteorite strike, except the recoil is so violent the disciple firing it often gets blasted into the wall and can't be pried out.
16663: Learn to make the ultimate forms of battle armor and mecha. Powered by Star Energy, forged from meteoric iron and black steel with star-vein channels built in, their wearers can take on mountains.
16664: Unlocks giant mechanical beasts: black iron bones and Star Energy cores. Three zhang tall and able to carry ten thousand jun, but as slow as a tortoise, and the ground cracks three chi deep when they turn.
16665: Unlocks energy building structures, with a built-in "mechanical aesthetics" bonus. Deliberately aged for maximum weathered charm! Though archaeologists insist "this was built last week".
16666: Study the statue of a past master to raise martial attainment. The holy statue is carved with ancient Dao patterns, turning "a clay figure" into "the Dao made manifest". In the end, martial arts are passed down by getting beaten!
16667: Unlocks the Sword Jade Tablet. Studying its ancient sword marks raises sword attainment; sword intent resonates with the mind method, triggering a state of "person and sword in harmony" that nurtures body and mind.
16668: Unlocks the Taixuan Jade Disc. Touching the Dao patterns on it raises disciples' Comprehension! Its qi nourishes the body, and some people get the illusion they're "made of iron" and go take a spiked club head-on.
16669: Learn to make more advanced prosthetics. A full set of advanced prosthetics working together rivals puppet mechanism arts in combat! It's just that taking them off to bathe takes three double-hours, and they need regular oiling.
16670: When spring returns and everything comes back to life, poplar is the first choice for many tree planters and garden lovers.

17420: An elephant train stops at the post station, the huge animals draped in colored silk, golden bells ringing in the wind. A foreign envoy asks for fodder in stiff Mandarin, and the stationmaster hurries his men to bring out the stores. As the white elephants curl up their food, their breath roars like bellows, and the horses in the stable neigh in alarm. The envoy's guards stand silent, curved blades in hand, watching the sun set over the Central Plains.
17421: A Western Regions caravan unloads rarities at the post station: yellowed sheepskin books and whole carvings of yellow rosewood. The bearded master runs his hand over a gilt spine and whispers mysteriously, "This is a secret tantric scroll." He taps a red sandalwood box, and as agarwood scent fills the air, it reveals ivory counting rods the color of jade. Scholars who know their stuff have already gathered to ask prices, fingers lingering on the antiques' patina.
17422: He has no sect. He learned martial arts from three different masters, each of whom taught him for half a year and then left. He didn't chase them; he blended the three styles into a way of his own. When people laugh at his untrained style, he says: in the jianghu, who isn't untrained? He makes a living escorting private goods and won't take killing jobs, says they're bad luck. Once he ran into bandits and didn't fight; he pulled out his rations and shared them, and when they'd eaten, everyone went their own way. Asked what he was thinking, he said: they're just trying to earn a living too. Not worth dying over.
17423: He joined the Cao Gang at fifteen, and in twenty years became the best fighter of the younger generation. Not through talent, but by training every night after everyone else was asleep. After training he'd sit by the river and watch the boats come and go. Someone asked what he was looking at. He said: the water. What's so interesting about water? "The water never stops, and I don't want to either." Later, when the gang chose an incense master, he was the youngest. On his first day in the post, he still went to sit by the river, and only went to bed after watching the water.
17424: I want to go back to Jingyun Mountain. Can you help me?
17425: I want to go back to Longhu Palace. Can you help me?

17460: It walks the gap between yin and yang, eyes empty yet seeming to hold endless obsession. Its flesh is rotten and its steps stagger, yet it closes in step by step, like time itself chasing oblivion.

17475: Legend says you're the Rain God reborn. Wherever you go, rain pours down, and it rains more often.

17494: Possessed by a Sword Saint at birth, and so begins the tale of a poor kid's rise to the top.
17498: You're very good at "receive, transform, release" and full of theory. If you're lucky enough to learn Taiji fist in the jianghu, it will be 100% more powerful.
17499: Doomed under the Lone Star: every 2 years, you face a crisis that could wipe out your sect. If you're lucky enough to survive, Aptitude +50; if any disciple dies, Aptitude +50 more.
17501: Central Plains martial arts are nothing special after all... You there, the boy with the defiant look on your face. Want a taste of this old man's golden wheel too?
17502: Seven days have passed. If that person still hasn't shown up, I'm afraid... there's no point waiting any longer.
17503: A group of out-of-control Mohist mechanisms has broken into this once-peaceful land, causing travelers a lot of trouble.
17507: The Way of the Sword Runs Deep
17508: Years of honed swordsmanship, reduced from complexity to simplicity.
